   c. If query result is also null, call Ordinal_10980(handle, 0) and return true
6. Initialize dwOrdinal10326 to 0 for parameter passing
7. Call Ordinal_10329(pdwItemData) to get secondary data value
8. Call Ordinal_10326(pdwItemData) to get primary ordinal value
9. Call Ordinal_10216 with entity field at offset 0x38, primary ordinal, secondary data, and zero
10. Call InitializeEntityDataStructure(nEntity, 4) to initialize entity with type 4 data
11. Call Ordinal_10980(validation handle, initialization result) to store result
12. Call Ordinal_10981(validation handle, first dword from item data)
13. Call Ordinal_10982(validation handle, third dword from item data at offset 0x8)
14. Return true for successful completion

Parameters:
nEntity (int): Entity structure pointer; accessed at offset 0x38 for nested structure reference

Returns:
bool: false if entity validation fails (Ordinal_10323 returns 0); true otherwise

Special Cases:
Magic number 0x8cb passed to FUN_6fb8d210 (decimal 2251) - likely entity type or operation code
Query parameters 0xffffffff (all items), 4 (item type), 4 (query mode) when no existing data
Item data structure has dwords at offsets 0x0 and 0x8 extracted and stored via ordinal functions
Early return with true when validation succeeds but query returns no results

Item Data Structure Layout:
Offset  Size  Field Name              Type   Description
0x00    0x4   dwItemField0            uint   First item parameter stored via Ordinal_10981
0x04    0x4   dwItemField1            uint   Second field (not directly accessed)
0x08    0x4   dwItemField2            uint   Third item parameter stored via Ordinal_10982

functions.name: ConsumeItemCharge
functions.comment:
Consume one charge from an item with charges and apply associated effects.

Algorithm:

1. Retrieve charge state object from unit
2. Get current charge index and item type from charge state
3. Search for existing charge item using type and index
4. If no charge item found, execute item query to find it
5. If still no item found after query, return early (no charges available)
6. Get current charge count from charge state
7. Decrement charge count by 1 and update charge state
8. If remaining charges > 0, execute item query for next charge item
9. If next charge item found:
   - Get item X and Y coordinates
   - Perform operation on unit's memory pool with coordinates and zero flag
   - Update charge state with item's first and third dword values
   - Retrieve updated charge state object
   - Get damage value from charge state
   - Apply damage reduction to unit with damage value
   - Get skill/effect type
   - Execute skill effect with unit and zero parameters
10. Return

Parameters:

pUnit - Pointer to UnitAny structure representing the unit consuming charges

Returns:

void - No return value

Special Cases:

- If no charge item exists initially, attempts to find via item query before failing
- If charge count becomes 0 or negative after decrement, skips effect application
- If item query for next charge fails, skips effect application phase
- Uses zero-initialized float and int parameters for final skill execution

Magic Numbers Reference:

0x4 (4 decimal) - Item query criteria flag
0x4 (4 decimal) - Item query flags parameter
0x0 (0 decimal) - Zero flag parameter for coordinate operation
0x38 (56 decimal) - Offset to pMemPool field in UnitAny structure

functions.name: ExecuteAmazonSkill
functions.signature: void ExecuteAmazonSkill(UnitAny * pUnit, int nSkillId, uint dwFlags)
functions.comment:
Execute Amazon character class skill with validation and missile targeting.

Algorithm:
1. Validate skill has execution permission via Ordinal_10323(pUnit)
2. Calculate skill table index: nSkillIndex = nSkillId - 6
3. Validate nSkillIndex in range [0, 30) - covers Amazon skill IDs 6-35
4. If out of range, trigger assertion with error message and terminate
5. If no permission (fHasPermission == 0), return early without execution
6. Look up skill descriptor in g_AmazonSkillDescriptorTable at [nSkillIndex * 20]
7. If descriptor.dwTargetType != 0xFFFF, call CalculateMissileTargetCoordinates
8. Set unit flag pUnit->dwFlags |= 0x40 after missile targeting
9. If descriptor.pfnSkillHandler == NULL, set flag 0x40 and skip handler
10. Otherwise, call descriptor.pfnSkillHandler() with unit and flags
11. Retrieve audio context via Ordinal_10958(pUnit, 0)
12. If audio context exists, remove it with RemoveAudioContextFromList

Parameters:
  pUnit (ECX) - Pointer to UnitAny executing the skill
  nSkillId (EDX) - Skill identifier (expected range: 6-35 for Amazon skills)
  dwFlags (Stack[0x4]) - Execution flags passed to skill handler

Returns:
  void - No return value
  Terminates process if skill ID validation fails

Special Cases:
  - SKILL_ID_BASE = 6 (Amazon skill IDs start at 6)
  - NUM_AMAZON_SKILLS = 30 (0x1E) skill slots in descriptor table
  - Flag 0x40 at offset 0xE8 indicates skill execution state
  - Assertion uses format: "nSkillId >= 0 && nSkillId < NUM_AMAZON_SKILLS"
  - FUN_6fb9a10f(0xFFFFFFFF) is process termination after assertion

Structure Layout - Amazon Skill Descriptor (20 bytes, stride 0x14):

Offset | Size | Field Name      | Type        | Description
-------|------|-----------------|-------------|----------------------------------
0x00   | 4    | dwTargetType    | uint        | Missile target type (0xFFFF = none)
0x04   | 4    | pfnSkillHandler | code *      | Skill execution callback function
0x08   | 12   | (unknown)       | byte[12]    | Additional skill parameters

Magic Numbers:
  0x6 - SKILL_ID_BASE - Minimum valid Amazon skill ID
  0x1E (30) - NUM_AMAZON_SKILLS - Maximum skill count
  0x14 (20) - Skill descriptor structure size/stride
  0xFFFF - NO_TARGET - Indicates skill has no missile targeting
  0x40 - SKILL_EXECUTION_FLAG - Unit flag set during skill execution
  0xE8 (232) - Offset to dwFlags field in UnitAny structure
  0x293 (659) - Assertion line number in source file
  0xFFFFFFFF - Process termination error code

Error Handling:
  - Out-of-range skill ID triggers Ordinal_10023 assertion
  - Assertion displays: file path, line 0x293, condition string
  - Process terminates via FUN_6fb9a10f(0xFFFFFFFF) after assertion
  - No permission check returns early without error
  - NULL skill handler treated as valid (sets flag but skips execution)

functions.name: ProcessSkillParametersWithArea
functions.comment:
Process skill parameters and trigger area-based skill effects.

Algorithm:
1. Set flag bit 0x40 at pSkillEntity offset +0xe8 to mark skill as area-based
2. Allocate skill parameter buffer (0x100 bytes) using Ordinal_10594
3. Validate allocation succeeded, error if NULL with "ptSkill" assertion
4. Validate nParam2 field at buffer offset +0xf4 is non-zero, error if zero with "ptSkill->nParam2" assertion
5. Calculate total iterations: nIterations = (nParam2 - 1) / buffer[+0xf4] + buffer[+0xf0]
6. Calculate stride for area spread: nStride = nIterations / 3 using magic constant 0x55555556
7. Call ProcessSkillAreaPositions with effect type 0x184, calculated iterations and stride
8. Trigger skill event 0x103 using FUN_6fb8d210 with zero float parameters

Parameters:
  pSkillEntity: Pointer to skill entity structure with flags at offset +0xe8 (0x3a * 4 = 232 decimal)
  nParam2: Skill parameter value used for iteration calculation (skill level or area size multiplier)
  IMPLICIT EBX: Preserved through PUSH/POP for skill entity pointer backup
  IMPLICIT ESI: Preserved through PUSH/POP for nParam2 backup
  IMPLICIT EDI: Holds allocated buffer pointer from Ordinal_10594

Returns:
  void - Function applies skill effects as side effect through ProcessSkillAreaPositions

Special Cases:
  If Ordinal_10594 returns NULL, calls Ordinal_10023 with error string "ptSkill" at line 0x2e then exits with -1
  If allocated buffer field +0xf4 is zero, calls Ordinal_10023 with "ptSkill->nParam2" error at line 0x2f then exits with -1
  Division by 3 uses compiler optimization: IMUL with 0x55555556, right shift 31, add to get quotient

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x40 (64 decimal): Flag bit marking area-based skill processing at offset +0xe8
  0x100 (256 decimal): Size of skill parameter buffer allocation
  0x3a (58 decimal): Array index for flag field (byte offset 0xe8 = 58 * 4)
  0xf4 (244 decimal): Byte offset to nParam2 divisor field in allocated buffer
  0xf0 (240 decimal): Byte offset to base iteration offset field in allocated buffer
  0x184 (388 decimal): Effect type constant for skill damage area effects
  0x103 (259 decimal): Skill event code passed to FUN_6fb8d210
  0x2e (46 decimal): Line number for "ptSkill" null pointer error
  0x2f (47 decimal): Line number for "ptSkill->nParam2" zero value error
  0x55555556: Magic constant for division by 3 (computed as ceil(2^32 / 3))
  -1 (0xffffffff): Exit code for fatal assertion failure

Error Handling:
  NULL allocation check calls Ordinal_10023 (assertion handler) with source file and line number
  Zero nParam2 validation calls Ordinal_10023 with field-specific error message
  Both errors call FUN_6fb9a10f(-1) which terminates execution without returning
  Error messages reference C source: "C:\Projects\Diablo2\Source\D2Client\..."

Structure Layout:
  Allocated Buffer Structure (via Ordinal_10594):
    Offset  Size  Field Name       Type   Description
    +0xf0   4     nBaseIterations  int    Base iteration count added to calculated value
    +0xf4   4     nParam2Divisor   int    Divisor for nParam2 in iteration calculation

  pSkillEntity Structure (partial):
    Offset  Size  Field Name       Type   Description
    +0xe8   4     dwFlags          uint   Skill processing flags, bit 0x40 = area-based

functions.name: ValidateEntityStatePair
functions.comment:
Validates entity state consistency between two related game objects.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve related entity pointer using helper function FUN_6fb63760
2. If related entity is NULL, validation fails immediately
3. Call Ordinal_10342 on primary entity handle to get state identifier
4. Call Ordinal_10082 to check state validity (returns 0 for valid)
5. If primary entity state is invalid, validation fails
6. Repeat state check (steps 3-4) for related entity pointer
7. If related entity state is invalid, validation fails
8. Check first field of related entity: must be 0 or 1
9. If all checks pass, return 1 (success), otherwise return 0 (failure)

Parameters:
  nEntityHandle (int) - Handle or identifier for primary game entity to validate

Returns:
  1 (0x1) - Both entities have valid state and related entity type field is 0 or 1
  0 (0x0) - Validation failed: NULL related entity, invalid state, or type field not 0/1

Special Cases:
  - Related entity NULL check prevents dereferencing invalid pointers
  - State validation uses external ordinal functions (DLL imports)
  - Related entity first field (*pnRelatedEntity) constrained to binary values
  - Function has no callers in analyzed code (may be invoked via function pointer table)

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x0 (decimal 0) - NULL pointer check and valid state return from Ordinal_10082
  0x1 (decimal 1) - Valid type value for related entity first field and success return
  0x38 (decimal 56) - Offset used in helper function FUN_6fb63760 for entity field access

functions.name: ValidateAndTriggerObjectAction
functions.comment:
Validates object state and triggers action if conditions are met.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve first object pointer from context by calling FUN_6fb63760
2. Retrieve second object pointer from same context
3. Exit if second object pointer is null
4. Get value from context using Ordinal_10342 and validate with Ordinal_10082
5. Exit if validation fails (non-zero return)
6. Get value from second object using Ordinal_10342 and validate with Ordinal_10082
7. Exit if validation fails (non-zero return)
8. Read flag dword from second object at offset 0x0
9. Check if flag value is 0 or 1, exit if not
10. Check if first object pointer is valid, exit if null
11. Call FUN_6fb931f0 with first object and parameters (0xbe, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
12. Call FUN_6fb8d210 with parameters (0x950, first object, 0.0, 0.0, 0)

Parameters:
  nContext (int) - Context or parent structure pointer passed in ECX, used to retrieve object pointers

Returns:
  void - No return value

Special Cases:
  - Function exits early if second object pointer is null
  - Function exits if either Ordinal_10082 validation returns non-zero
  - Flag at offset 0x0 of second object must be exactly 0 or 1 to proceed
  - First object pointer must be valid to trigger actions

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0xbe (190 decimal) - Parameter passed to FUN_6fb931f0, likely action or message type
  0x950 (2384 decimal) - Parameter passed to FUN_6fb8d210, likely event or command code
  0x2 (2 decimal) - Third parameter to FUN_6fb931f0
  0x0 or 0x1 - Valid flag values at offset 0x0 of second object

functions.name: InitializeCompressionContext
functions.comment:
Initialize compression context with D2COMMON compression library.

Algorithm:
1. Create compression handle via Ordinal_10470 with parameters: type=0, mode=4, flags=0, first param, third param
2. If handle creation fails (returns 0), skip initialization and return success
3. Associate compression parameters with handle via Ordinal_10475
4. Retrieve error code via Ordinal_10993 with value 0x10e (270 decimal)
5. Configure handle with error code via Ordinal_10465 using property ID 0x44 (68 decimal)
6. Finalize compression context via Ordinal_10376
7. Always return true indicating function completed

Parameters:
  pCompressionParams - Pointer to compression parameter structure containing:
                       [0x0] First configuration value (passed to handle creation)
                       [0x4] Second configuration value (not used in this function)
                       [0x8] Third configuration value (passed to handle creation)

Returns:
  true - Function always returns success (1)

Special Cases:
  - If Ordinal_10470 returns 0 (NULL handle), initialization steps are skipped
  - Function returns true even if handle creation fails
  - No error propagation to caller

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x0 (Type parameter) - Compression type identifier
  0x4 (Mode parameter) - Compression mode (decimal: 4)
  0x0 (Flags parameter) - No special flags
  0x10e (Error code request) - Error code identifier (decimal: 270)
  0x44 (Property ID) - Handle property identifier (decimal: 68)

functions.name: SetPriorityByThreshold
functions.comment:
Set priority level based on threshold value with validation check

Algorithm:
1. Call FUN_6fb63760 to validate object and store result
2. Call Ordinal_10323 to retrieve handle identifier from object
3. Check validation result
4. If validation failed (result == 0), set priority level 0 and return success
5. If validation succeeded, determine priority level by threshold
6. If nThresholdValue <= 5, use priority level 1
7. If nThresholdValue in range 6-11, use priority level 2
8. If nThresholdValue >= 12, use priority level 3
9. Call Ordinal_10980 to apply computed priority level to handle
10. Return success (1)

Parameters:
  nObjectHandle - Handle or identifier to object for validation and configuration
  nThresholdValue - Threshold value for priority level calculation (compared against 5 and 11)

Returns:
  Always returns 1 (success)

Special Cases:
  - Validation failure results in priority level 0
  - Threshold boundaries: 5 (level 1/2 boundary), 11 (level 2/3 boundary)

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x00 (0) - Priority level for validation failure
  0x01 (1) - Base priority level for low thresholds (<=5)
  0x02 (2) - Mid-range priority level (6-11)
  0x03 (3) - High priority level (>=12)
  0x05 (5) - Lower threshold boundary for priority level decision
  0x0B (11) - Upper threshold boundary for priority level decision
  0x06 (6) - Start of mid-range priority (implicit)
  0x0C (12) - Start of high priority (implicit)

functions.name: ConsumeChargeAndApplyFullReduction
functions.comment:
Consumes one charge from unit's equipped item/skill and applies full damage reduction.

Algorithm:
1. Validate unit state by checking offset +0x38 is initialized
2. Retrieve charge reference (skill/item) from unit via D2COMMON ordinal 10323
3. If validation succeeded, query current charge count via D2COMMON ordinal 10976
4. If remaining charges > 1, decrement charge count by 1 via D2COMMON ordinal 10980
5. Apply 100% damage reduction to unit (nullifies incoming damage)

Parameters:
- pUnit: Pointer to UnitAny structure representing player/monster with charged item

Returns:
void - Modifies unit state in place

Special Cases:
- If validation fails (offset +0x38 null), early return without consuming charge
- If charge count <= 1, skip charge consumption but still apply reduction
- Charge reference (uVar2) is opaque handle from D2COMMON charge system

Magic Numbers:
- 0x38: Offset to validation field in UnitAny (checked by FUN_6fb63760)
- 100: Full damage reduction percentage (0% damage taken)
- 1: Minimum charge threshold before decrement (preserves last charge)

SSA Variables:
- iVar1 (fValidated): Validation result from FUN_6fb63760, then reused for charge count
- uVar2 (dwChargeRef): D2COMMON charge reference handle (undefined4 type)

functions.name: RenderAreaEffectByMode
functions.signature: void RenderAreaEffectByMode(RenderContext * pContext, int nCoordPacked, uint dwFlags, int nCenterX, int nCenterY, int nRenderMode)
functions.comment:
Renders area-of-effect visual effects based on skill mode and coordinates.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve primary skill data using GetSkillData1(0x103) where 0x103 (259) is skill ID
2. Retrieve secondary skill data using GetSkillData2(0x103) for same skill
3. Validate render mode is 2 (single effect) or 3 (dual effect)
4. If coordinates are packed (nCoordPacked != 0), extract X and Y using coordinate helpers
5. Render first area effect (ID 0x22c/556) at specified center coordinates
6. If mode is 3, render second area effect (ID 0x22d/557) with alternate skill data

Parameters:
  pContext - Rendering context structure pointer (RenderContext*) for effect system
  nCoordPacked - Packed coordinate value (0 if using explicit coordinates)
  dwFlags - Flags passed to area effect rendering function
  nCenterX - Center X coordinate for area effect (overwritten if nCoordPacked != 0)
  nCenterY - Center Y coordinate for area effect (overwritten if nCoordPacked != 0)
  nRenderMode - Render mode selector: 2 = single effect, 3 = dual effect
  IMPLICIT dwImplicitEDI - Additional parameter passed via EDI register to area effect function

Returns:
  void - No return value

Special Cases:
  - If nRenderMode is not 2 or 3, function returns immediately without rendering
  - When nCoordPacked is non-zero, nCenterX and nCenterY parameters are ignored
  - Mode 3 uses different skill data (nSkillData2) for second effect layer

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x103 (259) - Skill ID passed to skill data retrieval functions
  0x22c (556) - Primary area effect ID for first visual layer
  0x22d (557) - Secondary area effect ID for second visual layer (mode 3 only)
  2 - Single effect render mode
  3 - Dual effect render mode

External Dependencies:
  Ordinal_10990 - Retrieves primary skill-related data for skill ID
  Ordinal_10991 - Retrieves secondary skill-related data for skill ID
  Ordinal_10326 - Extracts X coordinate from packed coordinate value
  Ordinal_10329 - Extracts Y coordinate from packed coordinate value
  GenerateRandomPointsInRadius - Generates circular area effect at specified coordinates

functions.name: GenerateRandomPointsInRadius
functions.signature: void GenerateRandomPointsInRadius(void * this, GameContext * pGameContext, GameContext * pContext, uint dwEffectId, int nCenterX, int nCenterY, int nRadius, uint dwFlags)
functions.comment:
Generate random points within a circular radius and process valid locations.

Algorithm:

1. Store radius value in temporary variable for later use
2. Get context handle from pGameContext object via Ordinal_10342
3. Seed or initialize random number generator via Ordinal_10913
4. Calculate radius squared (nRadius * nRadius) for distance comparisons
5. Initialize local stack structure (88 bytes, 0x16 dwords) to zero
6. Set up structure fields:
   - dwStructFlag = 1 (initialization flag)
   - dwFlagsCopy = dwFlags (copy flags parameter)
   - dwEffectIdCopy = dwEffectId (copy effect ID)
   - pContextCopy = pContext (copy context pointer)
7. Loop nRadiusSquared times to generate random points:
   a. Generate random X offset: nOffsetX = nRadius - Ordinal_10918()
   b. Generate random Y offset: nOffsetY = nRadius - Ordinal_10918()
   c. Check if point is within circular radius using distance formula:
      if (nOffsetX² + nOffsetY² <= nRadiusSquared)
   d. Calculate absolute target coordinates:
      nTargetX = nOffsetX + nCenterX
      nTargetY = nOffsetY + nCenterY
   e. Validate location via Ordinal_10042(dwContextHandle, nTargetX, nTargetY)
   f. If location is valid (return != 0), process it via FUN_6fb77720(&local_58)
8. Return after processing all iterations

Parameters:

IMPLICIT pGameContext - Primary game context pointer passed via ECX register (__thiscall convention)
  NOTE: Auto-parameter 'this' cannot be renamed due to Ghidra __thiscall implementation
  Type: GameContext* (60164 bytes - contains game state, rendering, and resource management)
pContext - Secondary game context or data pointer
  Type: GameContext* (likely same structure or related context object)
dwEffectId - Effect or spell identifier (0x22c, 0x22d, 0x230, 0x231 observed)
nCenterX - Center X coordinate for radius calculation
nCenterY - Center Y coordinate for radius calculation  
nRadius - Radius value for circular area generation
dwFlags - Flags parameter passed to processing function

Returns:

void (no return value)

Special Cases:

If nRadius is 0 or negative, loop body never executes (0 < nRadiusSquared fails)
Random number generation uses rejection sampling - generates points in square bounding box,
  only processes those within circular radius using Pythagorean distance check
Number of actual processed points depends on collision detection and circle hit rate
  (approximately π/4 ≈ 78.5% of generated points fall within circle)

Magic Numbers Reference:

0x16 (22 decimal) - Stack structure size in dwords (88 bytes total)
1 - Initialization flag value for dwStructFlag

Structure Layout (88 bytes on stack):

Offset  Size  Field Name        Type      Description
------  ----  ----------------  --------  ------------------------------------
+0x00   4     dwStructFlag      uint      Initialization flag (set to 1)
+0x04   84    [remaining data]  byte[84]  Additional structure fields (not directly accessed)
        
The structure is passed to FUN_6fb77720 for processing valid locations.
The full structure layout and field meanings would be defined in FUN_6fb77720 analysis.

Implementation Notes:

This function demonstrates __thiscall calling convention with auto-parameter in ECX.
Completeness limited by auto-parameter 'this' which cannot be renamed (Ghidra limitation).

functions.name: CreateGameObjectByMode
functions.signature: void CreateGameObjectByMode(GameContext * pGameContext, int nDataRef, dword dwAdditionalData, dword dwUnused1, dword dwUnused2, int nModeSelector)
functions.comment:
Dispatches game object creation based on mode selector parameter.

Algorithm:

1. Validate prerequisites: mode selector must be 2 or 3, and data reference must be non-zero
2. If mode selector equals 2: Call Ordinal_10590 to retrieve control flags for magic number 0x22f
3. For mode 2: Create game object via InitializeGameObject with class type 0x22f, mode 0xffff (skip array copy), additional data, and control flags
4. If mode selector equals 3: Retrieve ordinal data results from data reference using Ordinal_10326 and Ordinal_10329
5. For mode 3: Create game object with sine wave data via InitializeTrigonometricTable using class type 0x22e, ordinal results, additional data, and stride value 4
6. Return if validation fails or after successful object creation

Parameters:

pGameContext (ECX): Pointer to game context or object container where new object will be created
nDataRef (EDX): Data reference or object source identifier used for ordinal lookups (must be non-zero)
dwAdditionalData (Stack+4): Additional parameter data passed to object initialization functions
dwUnused1 (Stack+8): Unused parameter (reserved)
dwUnused2 (Stack+C): Unused parameter (reserved)
nModeSelector (Stack+10): Mode selector determining object creation path: 2 = standard initialization, 3 = sine wave initialization

IMPLICIT: EBX register preserved across mode 3 path, passed to InitializeTrigonometricTable

Returns:

void (no return value)

Special Cases:

Magic Number 0x22f (559): Class type for mode 2 standard object initialization
Magic Number 0x22e (558): Class type for mode 3 sine wave object initialization
Magic Number 0xffff (65535): Mode parameter passed to InitializeGameObject to skip array copy operation
Magic Number 0x4 (4): Stride value for sine wave data processing in mode 3 path
If nModeSelector is not 2 or 3: Function returns immediately without creating object
If nDataRef is zero: Function returns immediately without creating object (validation failure)
Mode 2 path casts pGameContext from GameContext* to dword before passing to InitializeGameObject
Mode 3 path passes pGameContext as GameContext* directly to InitializeTrigonometricTable

Error Handling:

No explicit error codes returned; validation failures result in silent return
Caller must verify object creation success through separate means

Note: Function uses unaff_EBX phantom variable (preserved register) passed to InitializeTrigonometricTable in mode 3 path

functions.name: InitializeTrigonometricTable
functions.signature: void InitializeTrigonometricTable(void * this, void * pContext, int nTableType, uint dwParam1, uint dwParam2, uint dwParam3, int nStride)
functions.comment:
Initialize trigonometric lookup table with 128 sine/cosine values

Algorithm:
1. Populate 128-entry sine/cosine lookup table (0-127) with hardcoded values
2. Initialize trailing structure fields (22 uint entries) to zero
3. Save context pointer and copy input parameters to local variables
4. Set error label pointer based on table type (0x238 vs others)
5. Loop through table with configurable stride (nStride * 4 bytes)
6. For each iteration: extract upper/lower values from table entries
7. Call Ordinal_10918() with current values to perform operation
8. Call FUN_6fb77720() to retrieve object pointer from structure
9. If object exists and table type is 0x238, allocate memory and call Ordinal_11140()
10. Advance offset by stride and repeat until 256 bytes processed

Parameters:
  this - Object context pointer (passed in ECX per __thiscall convention)
  nTableType - Table type identifier (0x238, 0x22e, or other)
  dwParam1 - First operation parameter
  dwParam2 - Second operation parameter  
  dwParam3 - Third operation parameter
  nStride - Loop stride multiplier (controls iteration step size)

Returns:
  void

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x238 (568) - Special table type requiring memory allocation path
  0x22e (558) - Alternate table type using error label LAB_6faed240
  0x118 (280) - Size parameter for memory allocation in Ordinal_10991
  0x100 (256) - Total bytes to process in main loop
  0x80 (128) - Offset to structure fields / table entry count
  0x16 (22) - Count of trailing structure fields to zero-initialize
  0x40-0x7f (64-127) - Upper half of lookup table indices
  0x00-0x3f (0-63) - Lower half of lookup table indices

Special Cases:
  If nTableType != 0x238, pbErrorLabel points to LAB_6faed240
  If piObject is NULL, skip memory allocation/Ordinal_11140 call
  Stride determines iteration spacing: offset += (nStride * 4)

functions.name: GenerateMissileSpawnPoints
functions.signature: void GenerateMissileSpawnPoints(GameContext * pGameContext, int nEntityRef, uint dwRadius, int nCenterX, int nCenterY, int nSpawnMode)
functions.comment:
Generates missile spawn points based on entity position and spawn mode

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve two spawn type values (0x112) from ordinal functions
2. Check if spawn mode is 2 or 3, exit if neither
3. If entity reference is non-zero, extract coordinates from entity
4. Generate first set of random points (type 0x230) around center
5. If spawn mode is 3, generate second set (type 0x231) using alternate spawn type

Parameters:
  pGameContext (GameContext *) - Game context object passed as 'this' to GenerateRandomPointsInRadius
  nEntityRef (int) - Entity reference for coordinate extraction (0 uses provided coords)
  dwRadius (uint) - Radius for random point generation
  nCenterX (int) - Center X coordinate (or extracted from entity if nEntityRef != 0)
  nCenterY (int) - Center Y coordinate (or extracted from entity if nEntityRef != 0)
  nSpawnMode (int) - Spawn mode: 2 = single spawn type, 3 = dual spawn type

Returns:
  void - Spawn points generated via GenerateRandomPointsInRadius side effects

Special Cases:
  - If nSpawnMode is not 2 or 3, function returns immediately without generating points
  - If nEntityRef is 0, uses provided nCenterX/nCenterY directly
  - If nEntityRef is non-zero, extracts coordinates using Ordinal_10326/10329

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x112 (274) - Spawn type parameter passed to ordinal functions
  0x230 (560) - Primary missile spawn point type
  0x231 (561) - Secondary missile spawn point type (dual mode only)
  0x2 - Single spawn type mode
  0x3 - Dual spawn type mode

Ordinal Functions:
  Ordinal_10990(0x112) - Retrieves first spawn type value
  Ordinal_10991(0x112) - Retrieves second spawn type value
  Ordinal_10326(nEntityRef) - Extracts X coordinate from entity
  Ordinal_10329(nEntityRef) - Extracts Y coordinate from entity

functions.name: PlaySoundAndOverlayByType
functions.signature: void PlaySoundAndOverlayByType(int nSoundId, int * pOverlayTarget, int nEffectType)
functions.comment:
Plays a sound effect and creates a visual overlay based on effect type.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pOverlayTarget is not NULL
2. Switch based on nEffectType parameter
3. Case 1: Create overlay 0x11f with mode 2, play sound 0x8f9
4. Case 2: Create overlay 0x120 with mode 2, play sound 0x8fa
5. Case 3: Create overlay 0x121 with mode 2, play sound 0x8fb
6. Invalid type: Return without action

Parameters:
  nSoundId - Sound source identifier passed to sound system
  pOverlayTarget - Target unit/entity for overlay attachment (must not be NULL)
  nEffectType - Effect type selector (1, 2, or 3)

Returns:
  void - No return value

Special Cases:
  - If pOverlayTarget is NULL, function returns immediately without action
  - If nEffectType is not 1, 2, or 3, no overlay or sound is played
  - All overlays use mode=2 in FUN_6fb931f0 call
  - All sounds play at coordinates (0.0, 0.0) with param_5=0

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x11f (287) - Overlay ID for effect type 1
  0x120 (288) - Overlay ID for effect type 2
  0x121 (289) - Overlay ID for effect type 3
  0x8f9 (2297) - Sound ID for effect type 1
  0x8fa (2298) - Sound ID for effect type 2
  0x8fb (2299) - Sound ID for effect type 3
  2 - Overlay mode parameter (constant across all cases)

Function Pointer Context:
  This function is part of a dispatch table at 0x6fbb01e8
  Called indirectly via: CALL [EDI*4 + 0x6fbb01e8]
  EDI index determines which handler function executes

functions.name: DispatchOverlayEffectByType
functions.signature: void DispatchOverlayEffectByType(int * pEntity, bool fEnabled, int nOverlayType)
functions.comment:
Dispatches overlay visual effects and sound effects based on overlay type

Algorithm:
1. Validate fEnabled parameter is non-zero, return early if zero
2. Check nOverlayType value using switch-like logic (DEC instructions)
3. For nOverlayType == 1: Create overlay 0x122 and play sound 0x8ea
4. For nOverlayType == 2: Create overlay 0x123 and play sound 0x8eb
5. For nOverlayType == 3: Create overlay 0x124 and play sound 0x8ec
6. For all other values: Return without action
7. Call FUN_6fb931f0 to create overlay with mode 2 (no position params)
8. Call FUN_6fb8d210 to play sound effect at entity location

Parameters:
  pEntity - Pointer to entity structure (passed in ECX)
  fEnabled - Boolean flag to enable effect dispatch (passed in EDX, low byte DL)
  nOverlayType - Overlay type selector 1-3 (passed on stack at [ESP+0x14])

Returns:
  void - No return value

Special Cases:
  - If fEnabled is 0, function returns immediately without processing
  - If nOverlayType is not 1, 2, or 3, no overlay or sound is created
  - Each overlay type maps to specific overlay ID and sound ID pair

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x122 (290) - Overlay ID for type 1
  0x123 (291) - Overlay ID for type 2  
  0x124 (292) - Overlay ID for type 3
  0x8ea (2282) - Sound effect ID for type 1
  0x8eb (2283) - Sound effect ID for type 2
  0x8ec (2284) - Sound effect ID for type 3
  2 - Mode parameter for overlay creation (fixed position mode)

Note: Function uses phantom register variable in_register_00000009 (undefined3) optimized away by decompiler during EDX bool parameter handling

functions.name: ExecuteSkillMode
functions.signature: void ExecuteSkillMode(UnitAny * pCaster, int nSkillId, uint dwTargetX, uint dwTargetY, uint dwTargetId, int nMode)
functions.comment:
Execute skill with different firing modes based on mode parameter.

Algorithm:
1. Determine skill level: If nSkillId is 0, use dwTargetY as skill level, 
   otherwise call Ordinal_10326 to get skill level and Ordinal_10329 to get 
   target ID
2. Branch based on nMode parameter to execute different skill behaviors
3. Mode 1 (Single Missile): Fire single missile (ID 0x234) at target, set 
   light radius to 4 if missile has light, call FUN_6fb8d210 with code 0x985
4. Mode 2 (Trigonometric Table): Call InitializeTrigonometricTable with 
   missile ID 0x238, skill level, target coordinates, and count 0x10
5. Mode 3 (Multiple Projectiles): Get projectile count (0x118), seed RNG, 
   initialize missile structure with mode=3, loop to spawn projectiles at 
   random offsets

Parameters:
  pCaster - Pointer to caster unit entity
  nSkillId - Skill identifier (0 means use dwTargetY as skill level directly)
  dwTargetX - Target X coordinate or target entity ID
  dwTargetY - Target Y coordinate or skill level (if nSkillId is 0)
  dwTargetId - Target entity ID or target Y coordinate
  nMode - Execution mode: 1=single missile with light, 2=trigonometric pattern, 
          3=random projectile spread
  IMPLICIT unaff_EDI - Unknown implicit EDI parameter passed to 
                       InitializeTrigonometricTable

Returns:
  None (void)

Special Cases:
  - If nSkillId is 0, function treats dwTargetY as skill level instead of 
    coordinate
  - Mode 3: If both random offsets are 0, sets X offset to 0x14 (20) to avoid 
    spawning at exact center
  - Mode 3 initializes 0x16 (22) DWORDs on stack for missile structure

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x234 (564) - Missile ID for Mode 1 (single missile with light effect)
  0x238 (568) - Missile ID for Mode 2 (trigonometric pattern)
  0x239 (569) - Missile ID for Mode 3 (random spread projectiles)
  0x985 (2437) - Effect code passed to FUN_6fb8d210
  0x88 (136) - Offset to LightStruct pointer in missile structure
  4 - Light radius value for Mode 1 missile
  0x118 (280) - Parameter to Ordinal_10994 to get projectile count
  0x10 (16) - Count parameter for trigonometric table
  0x16 (22) - Number of DWORDs to zero-initialize for missile structure
  3 - Missile mode value for Mode 3
  0x14 (20) - Default X offset when both random offsets are zero
  0x10000 (65536) - Multiplier for Y coordinate in packed coordinate value

Coordinate Packing:
  Final coordinate for Mode 3 is packed as: nOffsetY * 0x10000 + (dwOffsetX & 0xFFFF)
  High word contains Y offset, low word contains X offset

functions.name: ExecuteSkillEffectCallback
functions.signature: void ExecuteSkillEffectCallback(UnitAny * pUnit, int nSkillId, uint dwFlags)
functions.comment:
Execute skill-specific effect callback for Assassin skills

Algorithm:
1. Validate unit pointer using Ordinal_10323(pUnit)
2. Calculate skill table index: nSkillTableIndex = nSkillId - 0xFB (251)
3. Validate skill table index is in range [0, 0x1E) (0-29)
4. If out of range, log error and abort with exit code 0xFFFFFFFF
5. If unit validation failed, return early without executing callback
6. Check if missile target skill ID is defined (not 0xFFFF) in skill params table
7. If missile target defined, calculate coordinates via CalculateMissileTargetCoordinates()
8. Set unit flag 0x40 in pUnit[0x3A] after missile calculation
9. Check if skill callback function pointer exists in params table
10. If callback is NULL, set unit flag 0x40 and skip execution
11. If callback exists, validate pointer is not bad code pointer via IsBadCodePtr()
12. If bad code pointer detected, log error and abort with exit code 0xFFFFFFFF
13. Invoke skill callback function pointer with no parameters
14. Retrieve audio context for unit via Ordinal_10958(pUnit, 0)
15. If audio context exists, remove it from list via RemoveAudioContextFromList()

Parameters:
  pUnit - Pointer to UnitAny structure representing the game entity executing the skill
  nSkillId - Skill ID value (expected range: 0xFB to 0x119, or 251-281 decimal)
  dwFlags - Flags controlling skill execution behavior (passed to CalculateMissileTargetCoordinates)

Returns:
  void - No return value
  
Special Cases:
  - If nSkillId < 0xFB (251) or nSkillId >= 0x119 (281), logs error and aborts
  - If unit validation fails (Ordinal_10323 returns 0), function returns early
  - If skill callback pointer is NULL, sets unit flag 0x40 but continues without error
  - If callback pointer is invalid (IsBadCodePtr returns true), logs error and aborts

Error Handling:
  - Out of range skill ID: Logs "nSkillId > 0 && nSkillId < NUM_SKILLS" assertion
  - Invalid callback pointer: Logs "sgpctSkillChartAssassin->nSkillId" assertion
  - Both errors call FUN_6fb9a10f(0xFFFFFFFF) which terminates process

Structure Layout:
  SkillParams table at 0x6FBA6D7C (30 entries, 20-byte stride):
    Offset | Size | Field Name           | Type      | Description
    -------|------|----------------------|-----------|----------------------------------
    0x00   | 4    | dwMissileTargetSkill | uint      | Missile target skill ID (0xFFFF if none)
    0x04   | 4    | pfnCallback          | void(*)() | Skill effect callback function pointer
    0x08   | 12   | (padding/reserved)   | byte[12]  | Additional skill parameters

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0xFB (251) - Minimum Assassin skill ID (base offset for table lookup)
  0x1E (30) - Number of Assassin skill entries in params table
  0x119 (281) - Maximum Assassin skill ID (251 + 30)
  0x14 (20) - Size of SkillParams structure in bytes (stride)
  0xFFFF - Sentinel value indicating no missile target skill defined
  0x40 - Unit flag bit set after skill execution or callback skip
  0x3A - Offset in UnitAny structure for skill-related flags (byte offset 232)
  0xFFFFFFFF - Exit code used for fatal assertion failures

Flag Bits:
  Unit Flags at pUnit[0x3A]:
    Bit | Hex  | Meaning
    ----|------|----------------------------------------------------------
    6   | 0x40 | Skill effect executed or callback skipped flag

functions.name: InitializeObjectConfigWithStride
functions.comment:
Initializes game object configuration with calculated stride-based offset.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve stride value from ordinal table entry 0x82 (130 decimal) via Ordinal_10990
2. Retrieve base offset from ordinal table entry 0x94 (148 decimal) via Ordinal_10590
3. Set configuration flag bit 0x40 in object flags field at offset +0xe8
4. Calculate final offset: stride * (index - 1) + base offset
5. Call InitializeGameObject with object pointer, class type 0x94, mode 0xffff, index value, and calculated offset

Parameters:
- pObjectBase (ECX): Pointer to game object base structure with flags at offset +0xe8
- nIndexValue (EDX): Index value for stride calculation (1-based index)

Returns:
- void (no return value)

Special Cases:
- Magic Number 0x82 (130): Ordinal table entry for stride lookup
- Magic Number 0x94 (148): Ordinal table entry for base offset lookup; also used as class type parameter
- Magic Number 0x40 (64): Flag bit set in object configuration flags (bit 6)
- Magic Number 0xffff (65535): Mode selector indicating no array copy in InitializeGameObject
- Offset 0xe8 (232): Location of object configuration flags field in structure
- Stride Calculation: stride * (index - 1) + base_offset produces element offset for array-like structure access

functions.name: PlayValidatedSound
functions.comment:
Validates sound system initialization and plays a hardcoded sound effect.

Algorithm:
1. Validate context handle by calling validation function
2. If validation succeeds, check if sound system is available via external ordinal
3. If sound system available, play sound with ID 0x9c0 (2496 decimal)
4. Return success (1) if sound played, failure (0) if validation failed

Parameters:
  nContextHandle (int) - Context or handle passed to validation function, likely game state or sound context
  
Returns:
  1 (true) - Sound validation and playback succeeded
  0 (false) - Sound validation failed or sound system unavailable
  
Special Cases:
  - Returns 0 immediately if initial context validation fails
  - Returns 0 if external sound system ordinal check fails
  - Always calls FUN_6fb8d210 with hardcoded parameters: sound ID 0x9c0, x/y coordinates 0.0, instance param 0

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x9c0 (2496 decimal) - Hardcoded sound effect ID passed to playback function

functions.name: InitializeObjectWithSound
functions.comment:
Initialize game object and play activation sound effect.

Algorithm:

1. Set bit 0x40 in flags field at offset 0xe8 of input object
2. Retrieve related object reference by calling FUN_6fb63760 with pObject
3. If related object pointer is not NULL:
   a. Call FUN_6fb7afc0 with pRelatedObject and zero parameter (positioning/movement function)
   b. Play sound effect 0x9c3 using FUN_6fb8d210 with pRelatedObject as position source
   c. Pass zero coordinates (0.0, 0.0) and zero extra parameter to sound function

Parameters:

pObject - Pointer to game object structure being initialized (GameObjectWithFlags *)
          IMPLICIT: ECX register (fastcall convention)
          Structure Requirements: Must contain dwFlags field at offset +0xe8

Returns:

void - No return value

Special Cases:

If FUN_6fb63760 returns NULL, sound playback and positioning calls are skipped.
Only the flag bit 0x40 is set on the input object in this case.

Magic Numbers Reference:

0xe8 (232 decimal) - Offset to dwFlags field in GameObjectWithFlags structure
0x40 (64 decimal, bit 6) - Flag bit being set to mark object as initialized/active
0x9c3 (2499 decimal) - Sound effect ID for activation sound
0.0 (float) - Default X and Y coordinates passed to sound function (uses object position)

Structure Layout:

Offset | Size | Field Name | Type    | Description
-------|------|------------|---------|----------------------------------
0x00   | 232  | padding    | byte[]  | Unknown preceding fields
0xe8   | 4    | dwFlags    | uint    | Object state flags (bit 6 = initialized)

functions.name: InitializeGameObjectWithOrdinalData
functions.comment:
Initializes a game object by setting ordinal-based flags and calling core initialization with calculated data offsets.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve ordinal data structure #1 for class type 0x95 (skill data tables)
2. Set bit 0x40 in game object flags at offset 0xe8 (enable ordinal-based processing)
3. Retrieve ordinal data structure #2 for class type 0x95
4. Calculate data offset using stride from ordinal data #1 at offset 0x78
5. Call InitializeGameObject with object pointer, class type, mode, index, and calculated offset

Parameters:
- pGameObject (ECX): Pointer to GameObject structure to initialize
- nOrdinalIndex (EDX): One-based ordinal index for data lookup (1-N range)

Returns:
- void (no return value)

Special Cases:
- Magic Number 0x95 (149): Class type identifier passed to ordinal lookup functions
- Magic Number 0x40 (64): Flag bit set at offset 0xe8 to enable ordinal processing mode
- Magic Number 0xffff (65535): Mode selector passed to InitializeGameObject (skip array copy mode)
- Offset 0xe8: GameObject flags field modified via bitwise OR
- Offset 0x78: Stride value in ordinal data structure #1 used for array indexing

Algorithm Verification:
- Step 1 maps to 0x6faed8fc: CALL Ordinal_10589 with 0x95 parameter
- Step 2 maps to 0x6faed903-0x6faed910: MOV/OR/MOV sequence modifying [pGameObject+0xe8]
- Step 3 maps to 0x6faed916: CALL Ordinal_10590 with 0x95 parameter
- Step 4 maps to 0x6faed91b-0x6faed924: Load stride, multiply by (index-1), add to base
- Step 5 maps to 0x6faed936: CALL InitializeGameObject with 6 parameters

Index Calculation:
- Formula: pOrdinalData2 + (stride * (nOrdinalIndex - 1))
- stride = *(int *)(pOrdinalData1 + 0x78)
- Converts 1-based index to zero-based offset
- Multiplies by stride to get byte offset into data array
- Adds base address from pOrdinalData2 to get final pointer

functions.name: PlayHitClassResistanceSound
functions.comment:
Plays resistance-based sound effect for hit class damage calculation.

Algorithm:

1. Call Ordinal_10365() to get current hit class type (physical, fire, cold, etc.)
2. Call FUN_6fb868b0(pUnit, hit class) to calculate resistance-adjusted damage value
3. Decrement resistance value by 1 and apply signed saturation mask
4. Call FUN_6fb8d210() to play sound effect 0x9c9 with calculated volume:
   - Sound ID: 0x9c9 (2505 decimal)
   - Source unit: pUnit
   - Volume: Based on resistance-adjusted damage (float cast of (value - 1))
   - Pan: 0.0 (centered)
   - Flags: 0 (default playback)
5. Return 1 (success)

Parameters:

  pUnit (UnitAny*) - Pointer to unit structure being hit

Returns:

  int - Always returns 1 (success)

Special Cases:

  - Resistance value clamping: Uses signed saturation via SETS/DEC/AND pattern
  - If calculated value is 0 or negative, result becomes 0xFFFFFFFF after saturation

Magic Numbers Reference:

  0x9c9 (2505) - Sound effect ID for resistance-based hit feedback

functions.name: ProcessEntityAudioEffect
functions.comment:
Process audio effect for entity based on state flags.

Algorithm:
1. Extract entity flags from offset 0x44 and mask upper 24 bits
2. Check if masked flags value is less than 0x600
3. If condition fails, return early without processing audio
4. Initialize audio parameters: zero value, zero float, small float constant (0x4 = 5.60519e-45)
5. Call Ordinal_10365() to generate or retrieve sound identifier
6. Call FUN_6fb86850() with entity and sound ID to get audio context
7. Call FUN_6fb8d210() to process audio with context, entity, and float parameters
8. Call FUN_6faed9e0() to find target entity for audio effect
9. If target entity found (non-null):
   a. Retrieve parameter 1 from target entity via Ordinal_10329()
   b. Retrieve parameter 2 from target entity via Ordinal_10326()
   c. Call Ordinal_10216() with entity offset 0x38 value, both parameters, and zero

Parameters:
  pEntity - Pointer to game entity structure (int *)
    Offset 0x44 (index 0x11): Entity state flags (upper 24 bits checked)
    Offset 0x38 (index 0x0e): Handle or identifier used in final audio call

Returns:
  None (void function)

Special Cases:
  - If (flags & 0xffffff00) >= 0x600, function returns immediately without processing
  - If FUN_6faed9e0() returns NULL, skips Ordinal_10216 call
  - Magic number 0x600 (1536 decimal) appears to be audio processing threshold

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x600 (1536 decimal) - Audio processing threshold for entity flags
  0xffffff00 - Bit mask to isolate upper 24 bits of flags
  0x4 (5.60519e-45 as float) - Small float constant for audio processing
  0x11 (17 decimal) - Array index for flags field (offset 0x44 bytes)
  0x0e (14 decimal) - Array index for handle/ID field (offset 0x38 bytes)

Structure Layout:
  Entity Structure (accessed as int array):
  Offset  Size  Field Name       Type    Description
  0x38    4     entityHandle     int     Handle/ID used in audio processing call
  0x44    4     stateFlags       uint    Entity state flags (upper 24 bits checked)

functions.name: FindNearestItemByPriority
functions.comment:
Find nearest item to player unit by priority distance value

Algorithm:
1. Initialize tracking variables: get default item from FUN_6fb63760
2. Set min priority to 0xFFFFFFFF (max uint), max priority to 0
3. Get player unit coordinates via Ordinal_10326 (X) and Ordinal_10329 (Y)
4. Build query structure: zero 14 DWORDs at local_38, set field[0]=0x583, field[1]=5, field[2]=pUnit, field[3]=X, field[4]=Y
5. Create context handle via Ordinal_11094 and initialize with Ordinal_11096(handle, X, Y)
6. Execute item query via Ordinal_10401 with query parameters (handle, buffer, coords, mode=3)
7. Open query results with Ordinal_10403(buffer) to populate item array
8. Iterate through all items in result array (count in local_4c, array at local_60):
   - For each item pointer, validate accessibility via FUN_6fb63e80(pUnit, pItem)
   - Validate item state via Ordinal_10361(pUnit, pItem, 0)
   - If both validations pass, read priority value from pItem[2] (offset +0x8)
   - Track minimum priority item in local_74 (selected result)
   - Track maximum priority item in local_6c (fallback option)
   - Track last valid item in local_70 (iteration tracking)
9. Apply selection logic: if last valid item equals min priority item, use max priority item instead
10. Fallback: if no item selected, call FUN_6fb63760 to get default item
11. Cleanup: close query with Ordinal_10402(buffer) and release context with Ordinal_11095(handle)
12. Return selected item pointer

Parameters:
pUnit - Pointer to player unit entity requesting nearest item search

Returns:
Pointer to selected item entity based on priority criteria, or default item if no valid items found

Special Cases:
When last valid item matches minimum priority item (line 68), function selects maximum priority item instead
This prevents selecting the same item repeatedly when multiple items have identical minimum priority
If no items pass validation checks, function returns default item from FUN_6fb63760

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x583 (1411 decimal) - Query structure identifier/type code at offset +0x0
0x5 (5 decimal) - Query mode constant at offset +0x4  
0x3 (3 decimal) - Search radius parameter for Ordinal_10401 (3-tile range)
0xFFFFFFFF - Maximum uint32 value used as initial minimum priority sentinel
0x8 - Byte offset to priority field in item structure (pItem[2])
0xe (14 decimal) - Number of DWORDs to zero-initialize in query structure

Structure Layout:
Query Structure (56 bytes starting at local_38):
Offset | Size | Field Name       | Type  | Description
-------|------|------------------|-------|----------------------------------
+0x0   | 4    | dwTypeCode       | uint  | Query type identifier (0x583)
+0x4   | 4    | dwMode           | uint  | Query mode constant (5)
+0x8   | 4    | pPlayerUnit      | int*  | Pointer to requesting player unit
+0xC   | 4    | dwUnitX          | uint  | Player X coordinate
+0x10  | 4    | dwUnitY          | uint  | Player Y coordinate
+0x14  | 40   | Reserved         | byte  | Additional query parameters (zeroed)

functions.name: PlayHitSound
functions.comment:
Play hit sound effect for unit when damaged

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve current game timer/tick value via Ordinal_10365
2. Calculate hit class-based sound volume using FUN_6fb868b0 with unit and timer value
3. Subtract 3 from calculated value and apply sign-extension mask for volume normalization
4. Queue sound effect 0x9cc (2508) via FUN_6fb8d210 with normalized volume
5. Return success (1)

Parameters:
- pUnit: UnitAny * - Pointer to unit entity that was hit

Returns:
- bool (always 1/true) - Success indicator

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x9cc (2508): Hit sound effect identifier
- 0x3: Volume adjustment offset for hit class calculation
- 0.0: Initial sound position offset (uses unit position from pUnit)

functions.name: ValidateAndPlayClientSound
functions.comment:
Validates client context and plays a specific sound effect if validation succeeds.

Algorithm:
1. Validate client context path by calling FUN_6fb63760(nClientContext)
2. If validation fails (returns 0), jump to return_failure
3. Validate sound system availability by calling Ordinal_11019(nValidationResult)
4. If sound system unavailable (returns 0), jump to return_failure
5. Play sound effect 0x9c0 (2496 decimal) via FUN_6fb8d210 with:
   - Sound ID: 0x9c0
   - Client context: nClientContext
   - Position X: 0.0
   - Position Y: 0.0
   - Flags: 0
6. Return 1 (success)
7. return_failure: Return 0 (failure)

Parameters:
- nClientContext (int in ECX): Client context handle or pointer, passed through to sound system

Returns:
- 1 (true): Sound validation and playback succeeded
- 0 (false): Validation failed or sound system unavailable

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x9c0 (2496): Sound effect ID for client-specific event

Special Cases:
- Function short-circuits on first validation failure
- Both client path and sound system must be available for sound playback
- Sound plays at origin (0.0, 0.0) with no special flags

functions.name: ReleaseAssociatedObjectAndNotify
functions.comment:
Release associated object from game entity and send notification event.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve associated object pointer from game object via FUN_6fb63760
2. Set flag bit 0x40 (64 decimal) at offset 0xe8 (232 decimal) in game object flags field
3. Validate retrieved object pointer is non-NULL
4. Call D2COMMON.Ordinal_10359 to validate object state
5. If validation succeeds (non-zero return), proceed with cleanup
6. Call FUN_6fb7afc0 with object pointer and 0 to release/cleanup object
7. Send game event notification 0x9c3 (2499 decimal) with game object as parameter

Parameters:
  pGameObject - Pointer to GameObjectWithFlags structure (236 bytes) containing entity data
                Parameter passed via ECX register (__fastcall convention)

Returns:
  void - No return value

Special Cases:
  - If associated object pointer is NULL, function returns early without cleanup
  - If D2COMMON.Ordinal_10359 validation fails (returns 0), cleanup is skipped
  - Flag 0x40 is set regardless of whether associated object exists or validation succeeds
  - Event 0x9c3 is only triggered if both object exists and validation passes

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x40 (hex) = 64 (decimal) - Flag bit set at offset 0xe8 to mark state change
  0xe8 (hex) = 232 (decimal) - Offset to flags field in GameObjectWithFlags structure
  0x9c3 (hex) = 2499 (decimal) - Game event notification ID for object release

functions.name: AutoPickupNearestItem
functions.comment:
Automatically picks up the nearest item if player state allows it.

Algorithm:
1. Check if player flags at offset 0x44 (masked with 0xffffff00) are less than 0x600
2. If check passes, initialize search parameters with 4.0 pixel radius
3. Call Ordinal_10365() to get pickup radius configuration
4. Call FUN_6fb86850 to get target entity for player
5. Call FUN_6fb8d210 to perform entity search/validation with radius parameters
6. Call FindNearestItemByPriority to locate the nearest prioritized item
7. If item found, get item coordinates via Ordinal_10329 (X) and Ordinal_10326 (Y)
8. Call Ordinal_10216 with player's entity handle at offset 0x38 and item coordinates to execute pickup

Parameters:
  pPlayerUnit - Pointer to player unit structure (int *)
    Offset 0x38 (56 bytes): Entity handle for pickup command
    Offset 0x44 (68 bytes): Player state flags checked against 0x600 threshold

Returns:
  void - No return value

Special Cases:
  - If player flags >= 0x600, function returns immediately without attempting pickup
  - If FindNearestItemByPriority returns NULL, no pickup is attempted
  - Search radius initialized to 4.0 pixels (0x00000004 as float = 5.60519e-45)

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x44 (68 decimal) - Offset to player state flags in unit structure
  0xffffff00 - Mask for extracting high 24 bits of flags
  0x600 (1536 decimal) - Threshold value for pickup eligibility check
  0x38 (56 decimal) - Offset to entity handle in unit structure
  0x11 (17 decimal) - Array index equivalent to offset 0x44 (17 * 4 = 68 bytes)
  0x0e (14 decimal) - Array index equivalent to offset 0x38 (14 * 4 = 56 bytes)
  5.60519e-45 - Float representation of integer 4 (search radius in pixels)

functions.name: InitializeUnitGraphicsContext
functions.comment:
Initialize graphics rendering context for a unit entity.

Algorithm:

1. Retrieve graphics data handle from unit structure (offset 0x38)
2. Query graphics context dimensions (width and height)
3. Store unit type from unit structure base field
4. Configure graphics context with command 0x1101
5. Initialize graphics data with zero coordinates (twice)
6. Set graphics viewport with queried dimensions
7. Set graphics mode parameter to 9
8. Determine alpha/transparency based on unit type:
   - Type 1 (Player): Read alpha from unit data at offset 0x1a0 (uint)
   - Other types: Read alpha from unit data at offset 0x41 (byte)
9. Apply alpha value (shifted left 8 bits) to graphics data
10. Bind graphics data to unit pointer with zero flags

Parameters:

  pUnit - Pointer to UnitAny structure containing entity data
  dwGraphicsContext - Graphics rendering context handle from Ordinal_10949/10950

Returns:

  void - No return value

Special Cases:

  - Unit type 1 treated specially with different data structure and alpha offset
  - Alpha value from byte sources expanded to match uint format via left shift
  - Graphics data handle stored at UnitAny offset 0x38 (field index 14)

Magic Numbers Reference:

  0x1101 - Graphics context configuration command
  0 - Initial coordinate values for graphics data
  9 - Graphics rendering mode parameter
  0x38 (offset 0xe * 4) - Graphics data handle field in UnitAny
  0x1a0 - Alpha field offset in player unit data structure
  0x41 - Alpha field offset in non-player unit data structure
  8 (shift) - Bit shift to align byte alpha to uint format

Structure Field Access:

  UnitAny:
    +0x00 (offset 0) - dwUnitType (type discriminator: 1=Player, other=NPC/Object)
    +0x04 (offset 1) - pUnitData (pointer to type-specific data structure)
    +0x38 (offset 14) - pGraphicsData (graphics rendering data handle)

functions.name: CalculateAndSetPathVelocity
functions.comment:
Calculate and apply path velocity for unit movement based on distance and velocity table

Algorithm:

1. Retrieve unit field data at offset 0x38 from unit structure
2. Extract X and Y coordinates from dwUnknownId parameter using Ordinal_10976 and Ordinal_10977
3. Get velocity-related value from unit field using Ordinal_10147
4. Validate velocity value bits 8-15 is non-zero, abort with assertion if zero
5. Calculate path length using Ordinal_10398 with unit pointer and coordinates
6. Enforce minimum path length of 1 if calculated value is less than 1
7. Calculate velocity scale factor using formula path length << 16 divided by velocity value << 12
8. Clamp velocity scale factor to maximum by decrementing if greater than 1
9. Search g_aVelocityTable to find matching entry where nPathLength >= nThreshold
10. Calculate final velocity using entry multiplier times nPathLength plus entry base value
11. Enforce minimum velocity of 500 if calculated value is less
12. Call FUN_6fb979a0 to prepare unit for movement
13. Call FUN_6fb97b90 to set unit velocity with negated calculated velocity as Y-component
14. Call FUN_6fb97f00 to apply velocity scale factor to unit

Parameters:

  pUnit (UnitAny *) - Pointer to UnitAny structure receiving velocity calculation
  dwUnknownId (uint) - Encoded coordinate or identifier used to extract X and Y position

Returns:

  void - Function modifies unit state directly through called functions

functions.name: ValidateSkillTargetAndInitialize
functions.signature: undefined4 ValidateSkillTargetAndInitialize(uint * pUnit, uint dwGraphicsContext, int nSkillParam)
functions.comment:
Validate skill target coordinates and initialize skill execution context.

Algorithm:

1. Extract target X and Y coordinates from graphics context
2. Retrieve current unit position coordinates for comparison
3. Determine skill ID based on unit type (monster uses 0x23f, player uses actual skill ID)
4. Check if unit is already at target position
5. If not at target and unit can move, handle error based on unit type
6. If at target position, set skill preparation state and update coordinates
7. Handle post-validation setup based on unit type and skill
8. For Phoenix Strike, calculate projectile trajectory
9. Validate line of sight and collision detection
10. If valid target, setup graphics effect and return success

Parameters:

pUnit - Pointer to UnitAny structure being controlled
dwGraphicsContext - Graphics context handle containing target information
nSkillParam - Skill execution parameter (non-zero triggers animation)

Returns:

1 - Skill targeting validated successfully and initialized
0 - Skill targeting failed validation (not at target position)

functions.name: InitializeCompressionState
functions.signature: void InitializeCompressionState(CompressionContext * pCompressionContext, int nTargetX, int nTargetY)
functions.comment:
Initialize compression state and buffer parameters based on compression mode.

Algorithm:

1. Read compression mode from context structure (offset 0x0)
2. Read internal handle from context structure (offset 0x38)
3. Obtain compression handle via D2COMMON.Ordinal_10342
4. If mode == 1 (high compression mode):
   a. If target coordinates provided (nTargetX != 0 AND nTargetY != 0):
      - Get buffer pointer via D2COMMON.Ordinal_10210
      - Initialize compression with buffer size 0x100 (256 bytes) via D2CMP.Ordinal_10126
   b. Configure internal handle buffer size to 0x100 via D2COMMON.Ordinal_10182
   c. Set internal handle parameter to 0x3c01 (15361) via D2COMMON.Ordinal_10184
   d. Set mode value to 2
5. Else (low compression mode):
   a. If target coordinates provided (nTargetX != 0 AND nTargetY != 0):
      - Get buffer pointer via D2COMMON.Ordinal_10210
      - Initialize compression with buffer size 0x80 (128 bytes) via D2CMP.Ordinal_10126
   b. Configure internal handle buffer size to 0x80 via D2COMMON.Ordinal_10182
   c. Set internal handle parameter to 0x1c09 (7177) via D2COMMON.Ordinal_10184
   d. Set mode value to 7
6. Apply mode value to internal handle via D2COMMON.Ordinal_10185
7. Validate compression state via FUN_6fb63680
8. If validation returns non-zero, reset context via D2COMMON.Ordinal_10143

Parameters:

  pCompressionContext - Pointer to compression context structure
  nTargetX - Target X coordinate (0 = skip buffer initialization)
  nTargetY - Target Y coordinate (0 = skip buffer initialization)

Returns:

  void - No return value

Special Cases:

  - If nTargetX or nTargetY is zero, buffer initialization (step 4a/5a) is skipped
  - Mode value 1 triggers high compression with 256-byte buffer
  - Other mode values trigger low compression with 128-byte buffer

Structure Layout:

Offset | Size | Field Name         | Type | Description
-------|------|--------------------|------|----------------------------------
0x00   | 4    | nMode              | int  | Compression mode (1=high, other=low)
0x38   | 4    | dwInternalHandle   | uint | Internal compression handle

Magic Numbers Reference:

  0x100 (256) - High compression buffer size in bytes
  0x80 (128) - Low compression buffer size in bytes
  0x3c01 (15361) - High compression mode configuration parameter
  0x1c09 (7177) - Low compression mode configuration parameter
  2 - High compression mode value
  7 - Low compression mode value

functions.name: ValidateAndCorrectSkillAnimationSpeed
functions.comment:
Validates and corrects skill animation speed based on character type.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve current animation speed from skill data at offset 0x38 (dwAnimationSpeed field)
2. Calculate expected animation speed based on character type:
   - If *pSkillData == 1: expectedSpeed = 0x100 (256 decimal)
   - Otherwise: expectedSpeed = 0x80 (128 decimal)
3. If current speed matches expected speed, return immediately (no correction needed)
4. Query skill target information to get X coordinate bounds (min/max)
5. If no target found, set bounds to zero
6. Otherwise, extract min/max X coordinates from target data
7. Retrieve skill flags and unit GUID for correction context
8. Apply animation speed correction using Ordinal_10126 with all context data
9. Update skill data structure with corrected speed and bounds via FUN_6fb61180
10. Initialize compression state for skill animation data
11. Send skill update notification (opcode 0x36) to synchronize state

Parameters:
- pSkillData: Pointer to skill data structure (minimum 60 bytes)
  - Offset 0x00 (uint): Character type flag (1 = specific type, other = default)
  - Offset 0x38 (uint): Current animation speed value (dwAnimationSpeed)

Returns:
- void

Special Cases:
- If current animation speed already matches expected value, function returns early without corrections
- Character type 1 uses doubled animation speed (256) compared to default (128)
- If skill has no target (Ordinal_10323 returns 0), bounds are zeroed before correction
- Animation speed mismatch typically occurs after skill state changes or network desync

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x0E (14 decimal): Offset to dwAnimationSpeed field in skill structure
- 0x100 (256 decimal): Animation speed for character type 1
- 0x80 (128 decimal): Default animation speed for other character types
- 0xFFFFFF80 (-128 as signed): Bitmask for default speed calculation
- 0x36 (54 decimal): Skill update notification opcode
- 0 (parameter 3): Reserved/unused parameter in speed correction call

functions.name: ProcessUnitGraphicsContext
functions.comment:
Process unit graphics context based on current state flags

Algorithm:
1. Acquire graphics context handle with task ID 0xFFFFFFFF (current task)
2. Retrieve context state flags from graphics context
3. Read unit type from first field of UnitAny structure
4. If graphics context is valid (non-zero):
   a. Check if flag 0x100 (SKILL_VALIDATION_REQUIRED) is set
   b. If set, validate skill target and initialize graphics
   c. If validation returns 0 (failure), exit early
   d. Check if flag 0x80 (INITIALIZE_GRAPHICS) is set
   e. If set, initialize unit graphics context and calculate path velocity, then return
   f. If unit type is not 1 (not a player), release graphics context with flag 0x1000

Parameters:
  pUnit - Pointer to UnitAny structure containing unit data and type

Returns:
  void - No return value

Special Cases:
  - Early return if graphics context is NULL (0)
  - Early return if skill validation fails when flag 0x100 is set
  - Player units (type 1) skip graphics context release in final branch
  - Flag 0x80 and 0x100 are mutually exclusive execution paths

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0xFFFFFFFF - Current task ID for graphics context acquisition
  0x100 (256) - SKILL_VALIDATION_REQUIRED flag - triggers skill target validation
  0x80 (128) - INITIALIZE_GRAPHICS flag - triggers graphics initialization
  0x1000 (4096) - Context release flag for non-player units
  0x1 (1) - Player unit type constant
  0x84 (132) - Graphics context type parameter for Ordinal_10949

functions.name: ProcessUnitAIByGraphicsFlags
functions.comment:
Process unit AI behavior based on graphics context flags.

Algorithm:

1. Retrieve graphics context handle for current frame
2. Query context flags to determine required AI behavior mode
3. Early return if no valid graphics context exists
4. Check flag 0x100 (skill/item interaction mode):
   a. Validate skill target and initialize skill execution
   b. Return early if validation fails
   c. Retrieve item type and context parameters
   d. Search for valid target item (prioritize type 6 = gold/special items)
   e. If no item found via type search, use nearest item by priority
   f. If still no valid target, set unit action state to 0x400 (idle/ready)
   g. If valid target found:
      - Set unit target pointer to target item
      - Clear path state
      - Retrieve skill context parameters
      - Calculate path to target with zero coordinates (auto-calculate)
      - Initialize movement/path system for approach
5. Check flag 0x80 (graphics initialization mode):
   a. If NOT set, apply state flag 0x1000 to graphics context (standby)
   b. If set:
      - Initialize unit graphics context with current frame data
      - Calculate and set path velocity for unit movement
      - Return

Parameters:

  pUnit - Pointer to UnitAny structure representing the game entity

Returns:

  void - No return value (state changes applied directly to unit structure)

Special Cases:

  - Flag 0x100 and 0x80 can both be set; 0x100 is processed first
  - Item type 6 is special-cased for direct search failure fallback
  - Zero coordinates (0.0, 0.0) in path calculation trigger auto-targeting
  - State 0x400 represents idle/ready action when no valid interaction target
  - State 0x1000 represents standby/waiting mode in graphics context

Magic Numbers Reference:

  0x100 (256 decimal) - Skill/item interaction mode flag in context flags
  0x80 (128 decimal) - Graphics initialization mode flag in context flags
  0x400 (1024 decimal) - Unit action state: idle/ready for interaction
  0x1000 (4096 decimal) - Graphics context state: standby/waiting mode
  6 - Item type for gold or special pickup items
  0x15 (21 decimal) - Offset in UnitAny structure for action state field (pPath field at offset 0x54 bytes)

functions.name: SetGameObjectModeFlag
functions.comment:
Sets a mode flag on a game object and initializes it with specific parameters.

Algorithm:

1. Set bit 0x40 in the game object's flags field (offset 0xe8)
2. Initialize the game object with class type 0xeb and mode selector 0xffff
3. Call secondary initialization function with parameter 0xaa

Parameters:

pGameObject - Pointer to GameObjectWithFlags structure to modify
dwModeParameter - Mode-specific parameter passed to InitializeGameObject

Returns:

void - No return value

Special Cases:

Magic Numbers:
  0x40 (0x000040) - Flag bit enabling specific game object mode
  0xeb (235) - Class type identifier for object initialization
  0xffff (65535) - Mode selector value (all modes enabled)
  0xaa (170) - Secondary initialization parameter
  0xe8 (232) - Byte offset to dwFlags field in GameObjectWithFlags structure

Structure Layout:

Offset | Size | Field Name | Type  | Description
-------|------|------------|-------|----------------------------------
0xe8   | 4    | dwFlags    | dword | Game object flags (bit 0x40 = mode enabled)

functions.name: ConfigureObjectProperties
functions.comment:
Configure object properties based on validation and context mode.

Algorithm:

1. Validate object by calling Ordinal_10323 to obtain handle
2. Retrieve data context for object via FUN_6fb63760
3. Check both handle and data context are non-NULL
4. Validate data context with Ordinal_11020
5. Retrieve property values from data context (Ordinal_10326, Ordinal_10329)
6. Apply properties to handle (Ordinal_10980, Ordinal_10981)
7. Access nested structure pointer at data context offset +0x04
8. Call Ordinal_10582 to resolve nested structure pointer
9. Read mode byte from nested structure at offset +0x19a
10. Branch on mode byte value and call Ordinal_10982 with mode-specific property
11. Return success (1) if all validations pass, failure (0) otherwise

Parameters:

pObject - Pointer to object requiring property configuration

Returns:

true (1) - Object properties successfully configured based on mode
false (0) - Validation failed (NULL handle, NULL context, or validation check failed)

Special Cases:

Mode byte 0x02: Sets property 0xfc (252 decimal) - Binary mode configuration
Mode byte 0x03: Sets property 0xff (255 decimal) - Extended mode configuration  
Other values: Sets property 0xf9 (249 decimal) - Default/fallback mode

Structure Layout:

Data Context Structure:
Offset  Size  Field Name       Type      Description
------  ----  ---------------  --------  -----------
0x00    4     (unknown)        void *    Base pointer
0x04    4     pNestedStruct    void *    Pointer to nested configuration structure

Nested Structure:
Offset  Size  Field Name       Type      Description
------  ----  ---------------  --------  -----------
0x19a   1     byMode           byte      Configuration mode selector (0x02, 0x03, or other)

Magic Numbers Reference:

0xfc (252) - Binary mode property value
0xf9 (249) - Default mode property value  
0xff (255) - Extended mode property value
0x02 - Binary mode selector
0x03 - Extended mode selector
0x19a (410 decimal) - Offset to mode byte in nested structure
0x04 - Offset to nested structure pointer in data context

functions.name: RenderControlWithTransparency
functions.signature: void RenderControlWithTransparency(uint * pControl, uint dwColor, int nTransparencyMode)
functions.comment:
Renders a UI control with modified transparency/alpha blending.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve current alpha/light value from control structure at offset 0x38
2. Calculate modified alpha based on transparency mode:
   - Mode 0: Add 0x2A (42 decimal) for higher transparency
   - Mode 1: Add 0x15 (21 decimal) for lower transparency
3. Mask result with 0x3F (63 decimal, 6-bit mask) and apply temporarily
4. Check viewport state with Ordinal_10010
5. Calculate screen coordinates:
   - If in viewport mode (return != 0): Convert world coordinates to screen
   - If not in viewport: Get direct screen coordinates
6. Call rendering function FUN_6fb91fe0 with calculated coordinates
7. Restore original alpha/light value

Parameters:
  pControl - Pointer to UI control structure (offset 0x38 contains alpha/light value)
  dwColor - Color value or rendering flags
  nTransparencyMode - Transparency mode selector:
                      0 = Higher transparency (add 42)
                      1 = Lower transparency (add 21)

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Alpha mask 0x3F limits blending to 6-bit range (0-63)
  - Different transparency deltas suggest two visibility states
  - Viewport check determines coordinate system (world vs screen)
  - First DWORD of pControl checked for zero (control state flag)

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x38 (56) - Offset to alpha/light value in control structure
  0x2A (42) - Transparency delta for mode 0 (higher transparency)
  0x15 (21) - Transparency delta for mode 1 (lower transparency)
  0x3F (63) - Alpha channel mask (6-bit, limits to 0-63 range)
  0x60 (96) - Flags parameter for coordinate conversion function
  0x0E (14) - Array index for alpha value (56/4 = 14th uint element)

functions.name: LogAbilityErrorWithCriticalSection
functions.comment:
Logs ability errors while managing critical section synchronization state.

Algorithm:

1. Retrieve global critical section handle via Ordinal_10950
2. If critical section exists, check lock state flags via Ordinal_10985
3. If bit 0 (lock held flag) is set, set bit 1 (nested operation flag) via Ordinal_10984
4. Look up error handler by code 0x9e3 via FUN_6fb86ce0
5. Process error handler via FUN_6fb8d060
6. Send event notification (type 0x36) to unit via Ordinal_10486

Parameters:

  pUnit (UnitAny *) - Pointer to game entity experiencing ability error

Returns:

  void - No return value

Special Cases:

  - If critical section handle is NULL, function returns early without logging
  - Bit 0 in lock flags indicates critical section is currently locked
  - Bit 1 is set to indicate nested error logging during locked state

Magic Numbers Reference:

  0x97 (151) - Critical section identifier for ability error logging
  0x9e3 (2531) - Error handler lookup code for ability errors
  0x36 (54) - Event notification type for ability error events
  0x1 - Lock held flag (bit 0)
  0x2 - Nested operation flag (bit 1)

Error Handling:

  - Null critical section causes silent early return
  - Error logging occurs even if critical section is locked
  - Setting bit 1 prevents recursive error logging

functions.name: ProcessSkillEvent
functions.signature: void ProcessSkillEvent(UnitAny * pUnit, uint dwSkillId, uint dwParam)
functions.comment:
Process skill event for unit and execute associated handlers

Algorithm:

1. Validate unit context by calling Ordinal_10323(pUnit)
2. Calculate skill index by subtracting base skill ID (0x7E) from dwSkillId
3. Validate skill index range: must be >= 0 and < 0x1E (30 decimal)
4. If validation fails, trigger assertion with error message and terminate
5. If validation succeeds but unit context invalid, return early
6. Calculate skill table entry address: g_SkillEventTable + nSkillIndex * 0x14
7. Check missile target coordinate at table offset +0x0
8. If coordinate != 0xFFFF, call CalculateMissileTargetCoordinates and set flag 0x40
9. Retrieve callback function pointer from table offset +0x4
10. If callback is NULL, set flag 0x40 in unit flags
11. If callback is valid, invoke callback with (pUnit, dwParam) via __fastcall
12. Query audio context for unit via Ordinal_10958(pUnit, 0)
13. If audio context exists, remove it from list via RemoveAudioContextFromList
14. Return to caller

Parameters:

pUnit - Pointer to UnitAny structure representing the game entity
dwSkillId - Skill identifier (valid range: 0x7E to 0x9B inclusive, 126-155 decimal)
dwParam - Additional parameter passed to skill effect callback

IMPLICIT:
EBX - Preserved parameter value passed to callback function

Returns:

void - No explicit return value
Side effects: Modifies unit flags, removes audio context, invokes skill callbacks

Special Cases:

Skill ID out of range (< 0x7E or >= 0x9C): Assertion failure, program termination
Unit context validation fails: Early return without processing
Missile coordinate == 0xFFFF: Skip missile target calculation
Callback function pointer == NULL: Set flag 0x40 but do not invoke callback
Audio context == NULL: Skip audio context removal

Magic Numbers Reference:

0x7E (126) - Minimum valid skill ID (base skill offset)
0x1E (30) - Maximum skill count (valid index range 0-29)
0x9C (156) - Maximum skill ID boundary (0x7E + 0x1E)
0x14 (20) - Skill table entry stride in bytes
0xFFFF (65535) - Sentinel value indicating no missile target coordinate
0x40 (64) - Unit flag bit indicating skill event processed
0x3A (58) - Offset to flags field in UnitAny structure (byte offset 0xE8)
0x5E3 (1507) - Assertion line number in source file

Skill Event Table Layout:

Base Address: g_SkillEventTable (0x6fba6ff4)
Entry Size: 20 bytes (0x14)
Entry Count: 30 entries (0x1E)

Offset | Size | Field Name           | Type          | Description
-------|------|----------------------|---------------|----------------------------------
+0x0   | 4    | dwMissileCoordinate  | uint          | Target coordinate or 0xFFFF
+0x4   | 4    | pfnCallback          | function *    | Skill effect callback or NULL
+0x8   | 12   | (reserved/unknown)   | byte[12]      | Additional entry data

Flag Bits:

0x40 - Skill event processed or callback was NULL

functions.name: CreateMultipleShotMissiles
functions.signature: void CreateMultipleShotMissiles(UnitAny * pShooterUnit, uint dwMissileId, int nMissileCount, uint dwTargetX, bool fCollisionFlag, uint dwTargetY, bool fCreateTargeted)
functions.comment:
Creates multiple projectile missiles in a spread pattern from a shooter unit.

Algorithm:

1. Set shooter unit flag 0x40 at offset 0x3a (marks unit as missile source)
