13. Update skill array with correct skill level and re-render if threshold exceeded
14. Continue to next skill type

Parameters:
IMPLICIT EBP: Game data context pointer
IMPLICIT ECX: Window context (saved/restored from g_dwScreenWidth)

Returns:
void (no return value, state updated via globals)

Special Cases:
- Handles 6 maximum skill display slots via g_abSkillSlotFlags
- Supports 3-tier skill level display (uVar8, +1, +2)
- Skill display fails silently if textures unavailable (Ordinal_10257 returns 0)

Magic Numbers:
0x37: Screen width offset adjustment
0x28: Slot width (per-slot spacing in pixels)
0x9b: Base Y coordinate for first slot
0xc6: Alternate Y coordinate when condition met
0x1e: Y offset adjustment for condition met
0x80: Skill field offset for comparison
0x46: Skill parameter code (Ordinal_10519 parameter)
0x6: Maximum slot iterations

functions.name: DisplayPartyErrorMessages
functions.comment:
Display error/warning messages for all player classes in the party.

Algorithm:
1. Get game state and unit context via FUN_6fb62880()
2. Scan player class array g_aPlayerClassIds starting from index 0
3. For each class, fetch unit via Ordinal_10257() with game state ID
4. Skip if unit not found OR unit state invalid (Ordinal_10811 == 0)
5. Skip if unit is reserved/hidden (Ordinal_10767 returns 1)
6. Calculate error level (0=severe 1%, 1=warning 5-20%, 2=critical <1%)
7. Determine visual severity based on class type and internal state flags
8. Populate message buffer [0]=type, [1]=error code, [2]=severity, [3..]=flags
9. Call Ordinal_10072() to render message at screen position (width-60, Y-offset)
10. Move to next player class, repeat until boundary reached or error

Parameters:
(void)

Returns:
void - Messages displayed directly to screen buffer

Special Cases:
- If scan reaches boundary 0x6fbb760c, function exits cleanly
- Error severity calculation uses formula: (quality_stat * 100) / total_stat
- Message buffer size fixed at 72 bytes (18 dword elements)
- Y coordinate computed as g_dwScreenWidth - 0x3c or offset by 0x8c on error

Ordinal Mapping:
- Ordinal_10257: D2Common.GetUnit() - Retrieve unit by class ID
- Ordinal_10811: D2Common.IsUnitAllocated() - Check unit validity
- Ordinal_10767: D2Common.IsUnitReserved() - Check if hidden/reserved
- Ordinal_10567: D2Common.GetUnitLife() - Get health/state
- Ordinal_10731: D2Common.GetUnitStat() - Query unit stat (0x33=mana)
- Ordinal_10783: D2Common.GetUnitExtraData() - Fetch profession/type
- Ordinal_10519: D2Common.GetUnitData() - Get primary data (0x48=experience)
- Ordinal_10072: D2Common.DisplayString() - Render text on screen

functions.name: RenderSliderControlTemplate
functions.comment:
Render slider control template with position validation and formatting.

Algorithm:
1. Get current slider template pointer and screen coordinates
2. Initialize two Unicode string buffers (200 chars each)
3. Check if coordinates are within valid range (0x1e-0x6e X, screen_height-0x4b to screen_height-0xf Y)
4. If out of bounds: return immediately
5. If in bounds (normal case):
   - Get color value from position (mode 6: 0x80-centered)
   - Call Ordinal_10564 to get slider resource
   - Check unit data: validate (*[0] == 0) && ([12] != 0x11) && (-1 < color < 2)
   - If validation passes, set color to 1
6. Initialize third Unicode string buffer
7. Get alternate color value (mode 8: 0x100-offset)
8. Call Ordinal_10004 with color values
9. Format Unicode string using sprintf
10. Concatenate with in-stack string
11. Call Ordinal_10121 (render/draw operation)
12. Call Ordinal_10117 with calculated Y offset and zeros

Parameters:
None - uses global screen dimensions and slider control template

Returns:
void

Ordinal Functions Called:
- Ordinal_10565 (address 0x6fb2d763): Get slider template/resource handle
- Ordinal_10564 (address 0x6fb2d763): Get slider resource length/size  
- Ordinal_10004 (address 0x6fb2d7a6): Format color/position value to packed integer
- Ordinal_10121 (address 0x6fb2d7b8): Render slider control to screen
- Ordinal_10117 (address 0x6fb2d7da): Position slider with vertical offset

Special Cases:
- Coordinate validation uses screen dimensions from g_dwScreenHeight and g_dwScreenWidth
- Magic number 0x4b (75) is top margin, 0xf (15) is bottom margin, 0x1e (30) is left, 0x6e (110) is right
- Two rendering paths: out-of-bounds returns immediately, in-bounds renders slider
- Unicode string operations suggest wide-character rendering
- Stack-based temporary buffers (aUStack_190, aUStack_c8) for string formatting
- Note: Function uses stack-allocated temporaries optimized away in decompilation

Magic Numbers:
0x1e (30) - minimum X coordinate
0x6e (110) - maximum X coordinate  
0x4b (75) - top margin from screen height
0xf (15) - bottom margin from screen height
0x6f (111) - left boundary check offset
0x1f (31) - right boundary check offset
0x11 (17) - unit data validation constant
0x5f (95) - final Y offset calculation
100 - Unicode string buffer initialization count
6 - color mode for normal rendering (0x80-centered)
8 - color mode for alternate rendering (0x100-offset)

functions.name: UpdatePanelAnimationFrameWithValidation
functions.comment:
Validates and updates panel animation frame counter with timing constraints.

Algorithm:
1. Get frame data pointer (Ordinal_10519)
2. Determine panel type: 6=Inventory(fIsType6=false), 8=Character(fIsType6=true), 10=Spells
3. Fetch frame limit via appropriate ordinal (Ordinal_10564/10565/10566)
4. Return 0 if frame limit is 0 (invalid panel)
5. If frame counter < 2 (initial setup): initialize both current and previous frame values
6. If frame changed and count difference < frame_limit/8: update timestamp, store previous frame
7. Calculate frame range (7-15 frames) based on elapsed time
8. Apply animation interpolation if frame available and elapsed time < frame_range
9. Validate result (0 to frame_limit inclusive)
10. Return interpolated or constrained frame number

Parameters:
nPanelType (ECX) - Panel type: 6=Inventory, 8=Character, 10=Spells
IMPLICIT dwFrameDataPtr (EAX) - Frame data base pointer from GetUnitData

Returns:
int - Validated frame number (0 to nFrameLimit), or 0 on error

Magic Numbers:
0x10 - Offset stride for panel data structures (16 bytes per panel)
0x6fbf8fe0 - Base address of current frame values array
0x6fbf8fd8 - Base address of previous frame values array
0x6fbf8fe4 - Base address of frame update timestamps
0x6fbf8fdc - Base address of last frame change timestamps
0x03 - Mask for CDQ sign extension (rounding adjustment)
0x03 - Shift amount for frame limit division (divide by 8)
0x07 - Minimum frame range (7 frames)
0x0f - Maximum frame range (15 frames)

Related Functions:
- FUN_6fb62880() - Retrieves game unit/frame data
- Ordinal_10519() - D2Common frame index lookup
- Ordinal_10564() - Inventory frame limit
- Ordinal_10565() - Character frame limit
- Ordinal_10566() - Spells frame limit
- GetGlobalFrameCounter() - Gets current game frame counter

functions.name: RenderMainGameScreen
functions.comment:
Render main game screen with panels based on active game state.

Algorithm:
1. Check game type (Ordinal_10003 = GetGameType) - set dwExtraOffset=1 if type 3, else 0
2. Get scroll window mode (Ordinal_10005 = GetScrollWindowMode) - determines which panels to render (1=weather, 2=object, 3=both)
3. If scroll mode 2 or 3:
   a. Initialize anPanelData array (18 dwords, cleared to 0)
   b. Get or initialize ItemError panel resource using FUN_6fb5a050
   c. Render 5 item panels via Ordinal_10072 at positions (0,0), (0x100,0), (0,0x1e4), (0,0x229), (0x100,0x229)
4. If scroll mode 1 or 3:
   a. Render 5 weather panels via Ordinal_10072 at positions (400,0x3f), (0x220,0xfd), (0x2c9,0x1e4), (0x220,0x229), (400,0x229)
5. For weather/object panels based on scroll mode:
   a. If scroll mode 2: render object panels at bottom using g_dwScreenHeight adjusted by dwExtraOffset
   b. If not mode 2: render weather panels, report/clear errors from g_dwWeatherError, g_dwObjectError, g_dwItemError if set
6. Get mouse position (FUN_6fb8f680=GetMouseX, FUN_6fb8f690=GetMouseY) - returns nMouseX in EBX, nMouseY in EBP
7. Check always-run mode (GetAlwaysRunSetting):
   a. If disabled (0): check g_dwAlwaysRunModeEnabled for sprint state, set nRunMode=1 if enabled
   b. If enabled (!0): check g_dwAlwaysRunModeEnabled inverted, set nRunMode=2 or 3
8. Render movement mode indicator at bottom center via Ordinal_10072
9. Check if mouse in button hotzone [(ScreenWidth/2-0x91), (ScreenWidth/2-0x80)] x [(ScreenHeight-0x1c), (ScreenHeight-8)]
   - If yes: call FUN_6fb2e490 (handle button click)
10. Call UI rendering functions: FUN_6fb2dff0, FUN_6fb2e180, FUN_6fb2e2d0, RenderGameWindowElements, FUN_6fb2ef90, FUN_6fb2f200, FUN_6fb2f230

Parameters:
(none)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Panel array initialized to 0 before each panel type (local_110 is 18 dwords = 72 bytes)
- Array field [1] holds error code/panel ID, field [2] holds panel type indicator (0-9)
- Screen position adjustments account for resolution via g_dwScreenHeight and g_dwScreenWidth globals
- Magic number 0x91 and 0x80 define button hotspot left/right bounds on screen
- Magic number 0x1c and 0x8 define button hotspot top/bottom bounds from screen bottom
- Note: Function uses stack-allocated temporary abRenderBuffer[200] bytes optimized away in disassembly

Structure Layout:
anPanelData is 18-element int array used as parameter block for Ordinal_10072 rendering:
| Offset | Size | Field | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------|------|-------------|
| 0      | 4    | [0]   | int  | Reserved (always 0) |
| 4      | 4    | [1]   | int  | Error code or panel ID |
| 8      | 4    | [2]   | int  | Panel type index (0-9) |
| 12     | 4    | [3]   | int  | Reserved (always 0) |
| 16-68  | 52   | [4-17]| int  | Coordinates/flags passed to Ordinal_10072 |

Related Functions:
- FUN_6fb5a050() - Load panel resource by name
- FUN_6fb2e490() - Handle panel click event
- FUN_6fb2dff0() - Render viewport/map display
- FUN_6fb2e180() - Render character stats
- FUN_6fb2e2d0() - Render inventory items
- RenderGameWindowElements() - Render window frame/decorations
- FUN_6fb2ef90() - Render equipment display

functions.name: RenderLootExperiencePanel
functions.comment:
Render experience and loot progress bars on main game screen.

Algorithm:
1. Get current screen mode from FUN_6fb62880()
2. Update panel animation frame using UpdatePanelAnimationFrameWithValidation(6)
3. Query experience bar display status from Ordinal_10564()
4. If experience bar enabled, calculate bar height from frame count and divisor
5. Initialize panel data buffer (adwPanelData[18]) with values
6. Set panel color 0x1c (green) for experience bar
7. Query loot bar display status from Ordinal_10487(dwPanelMode, 100)
8. If loot bar enabled, calculate bar width from bar divisor 0x4a
9. Draw loot bar using Ordinal_10074() with color 0x1c or 0x1d based on mode
10. Draw experience bar using Ordinal_10074() if bar height nonzero
11. Query NPC damage status from Ordinal_10487(dwPanelMode, 2)
12. Draw NPC damage bar using Ordinal_10072()
13. Return to caller

Parameters:
None - operates on global screen state and panel variables

Returns:
void - modifies game display buffers

Special Cases:
- Experience bar color varies by mode (0x1c for mode 6, 0x1d otherwise)
- Loot bar drawn only if width > height calculation result
- Panel uses fixed screen height offset -0xd (13 pixels from bottom)
- Color modes: 0x1c=green, 0x1d=blue

functions.name: RenderItemStatBar
functions.comment:
Render item stat comparison bar on UI panel

Algorithm:
1. Get current animation frame timestamp via GetGameTick
2. Query animation panel update frame count
3. Retrieve item stat value (calls Ordinal_10565 = D2Common.GetItemStat)
4. If stat exists: calculate display width as (frameCount * 0x50) / statValue
5. Initialize 18-dword render buffer (local_48) to 0, set error type flags
6. Get elapsed time, query tooltip visibility via Ordinal_10487
7. If tooltip active: calculate stat bar progression percentage from elapsed time
8. Validate progressive bar width <= 0x50 pixels max
9. If progression < display width: query resolution mode, calculate X offset based on mode
10. Render comparison bar (old value) via Ordinal_10074 
11. Render error bar via Ordinal_10072 with NPC stat value
12. Clear tooltip and return

Parameters:
(void) - No parameters; uses global state for panel data

Returns:
(void) - No return value; rendering side-effects only

Magic Numbers:
0x50 - Maximum bar width (80 pixels)
0x6a - Panel widget type ID
0x1a - Elapsed time query parameter (26 ms)
0x70, 0x6f, 0x6e - X-axis offset calculations based on screen width
0xd, 0x9 - Y-axis offset calculations based on screen height
0x12 - Loop count (18 dwords for 72-byte buffer)

Related Callees:
- GetGameTick (via FUN_6fb62880) - Current animation frame
- UpdatePanelAnimationFrameWithValidation - Panel animation state
- Ordinal_10565 (D2Common.GetItemStat) - Query item stat value
- Ordinal_10487 (D2Fog.IsTooltipActive) - Check tooltip visibility
- Ordinal_10519 (D2Fog.GetElapsedTime) - Elapsed milliseconds
- Ordinal_10003 (D2Fog.GetScreenResolution) - Query resolution mode
- Ordinal_10074 (D2Fog.DrawBar) - Render colored stat bar
- Ordinal_10072 (D2Fog.DrawText) - Render stat label text

functions.name: RenderSliderGauge
functions.comment:
Render slider gauge indicator on main game screen.

Algorithm:
1. Query viewport object via FUN_6fb62880 and retrieve width/height from offsets 0xc-0xd
2. Extract viewport values: current value at 0xc, max value at 0xd, min value at 0xc
3. Calculate bar span: barEndPos = current - (current - 1), gives range of values
4. Compute offset: rangeValue = max < currentValue ? (max - currentValue) : 0
5. Initialize wchar_t buffer (100 characters) with Unicode constructor loop
6. Query mouse position: nMouseXPos = FUN_6fb8f680(), nMouseYPos = FUN_6fb8f690()
7. Validate mouse bounds: X in [width/2 - 0x92, width/2 - 0x17], Y in [height - 0x2b, height - 0x22]
8. If in bounds: format display string via Ordinal_10004, sprintf to buffer, draw label via Ordinal_10129
9. Check bar length nonzero, if yes continue to gauge rendering
10. For overflow check: if rangeValue > 0x226b901 then shift right by 7 bits
11. Calculate bar pixels: (rangeValue * 0x77) / barLength, clamp max to 0x77
12. Query slider width via Ordinal_10629, verify mouse within parameter bounds
13. Draw gauge lines: two horizontal white (0xff,0xff) lines at Y=(height-0x26) and Y=(height-0x25)

Parameters:
(implicit) viewport data via FUN_6fb62880 return - EAX contains viewport handle
(implicit) g_dwScreenWidth global - screen width for bound checks
(implicit) g_dwScreenHeight global - screen height for positioning

Returns:
void - renders gauge to backbuffer, modifies screen pixels

Special Cases:
Empty range: barLength == 0 skips gauge rendering
Overflow: rangeValue > 0x226b901 triggers bit shift scaling
Clamped: bar pixels > 0x77 reset to 0 to prevent overflow
Mouse out of bounds: conditional rendering skipped

Magic Numbers:
0x92, 0x17 - horizontal offsets from screen center for bounds
0x2b, 0x22 - vertical offsets from screen height for bounds
0x33 - vertical offset for label positioning
0x90 - alternate horizontal offset in gauge draw path
0x25, 0x26 - gauge line Y coordinates relative to height
0x77 - maximum bar pixel width (119)
0x226b901 - overflow threshold requiring bit shift
0xff - white color value for gauge lines
0x7 - bit shift count for scaling

functions.name: BuildKeyBindingDisplayStrings
functions.comment:
Build display strings for active key bindings in game UI

Algorithm:
1. Initialize Unicode output buffer (szOutputBuffer) with 400 Unicode characters
2. Initialize temporary stack buffer (dwTemp) with 30 Unicode characters
3. Call Ordinal_10004 (likely GetStringPrefix) to get prefix string
4. Copy prefix into szOutputBuffer via Unicode::strcpy
5. Lookup primary keybind ID for command 0x23 via LookupKeyBindingByCommandId
6. If keybind exists (wKeyBindId != 0xffff):
   - Clear temporary buffer via REP STOSD loop
   - Get string ID for keybind via GetKeyBindingStringId
   - Call Ordinal_10004 with string ID to get localized key name
   - Format into temporary buffer via Unicode::sprintf
   - Concatenate to main output via Unicode::strcat
7. Setup secondary keybind lookup (EDX=0, ECX=0x23)
8. Lookup secondary keybind ID via LookupKeyBindingByCommandId
9. If secondary keybind exists (wKeyBindId != 0xffff):
   - Clear buffer achTempBuffer via REP STOSD
   - Get string ID for secondary keybind
   - Call Ordinal_10004 with string ID
   - Format via Unicode::sprintf into achTempBuffer
   - Concatenate via Unicode::strcat
10. Calculate Y position: screen height - 0x17 (23 pixels from bottom)
11. Call Ordinal_10129 to render key binding display at calculated position
12. Return void

Parameters:
(none - implicit parameters via ESI/EDI unaffected registers)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- If primary keybind not found (0xffff), skips first binding display
- If secondary keybind not found, skips second binding display
- Uses both Unicode and ANSI string operations for compatibility
- Stack layout includes 0x1cc bytes allocated for Unicode buffers

functions.name: IsCoordinateInCenterPanel
functions.comment:
Determines if screen coordinates fall within the center game panel area.

Algorithm:
1. Load g_dwScreenWidth and calculate center panel horizontal bounds
2. Calculate left bound: (screen_width / 2) - 0x91
3. Calculate right bound: (screen_width / 2) - 0x80
4. Check if nScreenX >= left bound AND nScreenX <= right bound
5. Load g_dwScreenHeight and calculate vertical bounds
6. Calculate top bound: screen_height - 0x1C
7. Calculate bottom bound: screen_height - 0x8
8. Check if nScreenY >= top bound AND nScreenY <= bottom bound
9. Return 1 (true) if all four bounds satisfied, else return 0 (false)

Parameters:
  int nScreenX: Screen X coordinate (ECX in __fastcall)
  int nScreenY: Screen Y coordinate (EDX in __fastcall)

Returns:
  bool: 1 if coordinates are within center panel bounds, 0 otherwise

Special Cases:
  - Center panel position depends on runtime screen resolution
  - Bounds are fixed offsets from screen dimensions
  - Used for UI click detection

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x91 (145 decimal): Pixel offset for left edge of center panel
  0x80 (128 decimal): Pixel offset for right edge of center panel
  0x1C (28 decimal): Pixel offset for top edge of center panel
  0x8 (8 decimal): Pixel offset for bottom edge of center panel

Structure Layout:
  (Screen-space coordinates)
  Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
  N/A    | N/A  | nScreenX   | int  | Horizontal position in screen pixels
  N/A    | N/A  | nScreenY   | int  | Vertical position in screen pixels

functions.name: RenderSliderControlPanel
functions.comment:
Render interactive slider control panel for game settings/status display.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve current panel ID and animation frame timing (FUN_6fb62880, UpdatePanelAnimationFrameWithValidation)
2. Query panel height from external module (Ordinal_10566)
3. Initialize slider color to RGB(0xFF,0x00,0x00) red if not already set (Ordinal_10034)
4. Calculate effective panel width: if (height + 5 < frame_time) use frame_time, else check module status
5. Clamp width to valid range: 0 to (frame_time * 0x66 / height), minimum 0x19
6. Draw slider bar at screen position (center_x - 0x7f, bottom_y - 0x1b) with width and color
7. Query current mouse/cursor position (FUN_6fb8f680, FUN_6fb8f690)
8. Calculate animation progress: (frame_time >> 8) and (height >> 8)
9. Set animation state to 0 or 3 based on progress threshold and module validation
10. Initialize 200-char Unicode buffer for display text
11. Validate mouse cursor within slider bounds horizontally (center_x ± 0x7f) and vertically (bottom_y ± ~0x12)
12. If within bounds, format display text with GetStringResource and render via display callback
13. Call status update function with animation frame count

Returns:
void - Updates UI panel state and renders graphics to screen buffer

Parameters:
None - Uses global panel handle, animation state, screen dimensions

Special Cases:
- Panel width < 5 handled by clamping to zero
- Division by zero protected by < 1 range check before division
- Uninitialized color state handled by explicit RGB initialization
- Mouse position validation uses signed integer comparisons after scaling
- Note: Function contains 9 stack-allocated temporaries (uVar5, uVar6, iVar2, uVar1, uVar4, iVar3) optimized away by compiler

Magic Numbers:
- 0xFF, 0xF4, 0xC0, 0x4C: RGB color component values for slider appearance
- 0x10: Panel dimension constant used in calculations
- 0x66: Animation factor constant for width calculation
- 0x19: Minimum slider width threshold
- 0x7F: Horizontal offset from screen center
- 0x1B, 0x9, 0x12: Vertical positioning offsets
- 0x34: Y-offset for status message display
- 0x88: Module validation flag/status code
- 0xC8, 0x64: Buffer/iteration constants (200 bytes, 100 iterations for Unicode array)

functions.name: RenderGameStatePanel
functions.comment:
Renders game state indicator panel positioned near screen center

Algorithm:
1. Initialize parameter array (18 dwords) with zeros and game error state
2. Check if key state is set (FUN_6fb5d340)
3. If key set: Check mouse in button region relative to screen center
   - Valid region: [screen_width/2-8, screen_width/2+5] x [height-39, height-13]
   - If in region: state=3 (hover), else state=2 (out of region)
4. If key not set: Same mouse check, state=1 (active) if in region, else state=0 (inactive)
5. Call Ordinal_10072 to render panel with calculated position and state

Parameters: None (uses global screen dimensions)

Returns: void

Special Cases:
- Panel position: screen_width/2-8, screen_height-16 (top-left corner)
- Mouse region check applied regardless of key state
- State values: 0=idle, 1=active_hover, 2=inactive, 3=key_active_hover

Magic Numbers:
- 0x12 (18): Parameter array size
- 0x15: Key state constant
- 0x8, 0x5: Mouse region width adjustment (-8 to +5)
- 0x27 (39): Offset from bottom for region top
- 0xd (13): Offset from bottom for region bottom
- 0x10 (16): Vertical padding from bottom
- 0xffffffff: Color parameter (opaque white/no tint)
- 5: Unknown parameter (possibly layer/priority)

functions.name: RenderGamePanels
functions.comment:
Render active game panels and unit/monster selection displays.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize Storm/rendering subsystem with Ordinal_10127
2. Retrieve current game status handle via FUN_6fb62880
3. Extract game unit handle from status structure at offset 0x84
4. Validate unit handle with Ordinal_10257(handle, 8) - returns non-zero if valid
5. If invalid, set g_dwGameMode = 2 and return
6. If valid, verify unit type with Ordinal_10751 == 0x13
7. Check unit quality with Ordinal_10367 - abort if < 0 (invalid state)
8. Check input state flags FUN_6fb5d340(0x1f) and FUN_6fb5d340(0x9)
9. Set g_dwGameStateFlags based on game mode switch (modes 0-5)
10. Initialize local panel array [18] with zero-fill using REP STOSD
11. Set panel colors: red/green/blue/yellow to 0x80 via Ordinal_10034
12. Loop through 3 panels: if active in state flags, render label via Ordinal_10072
13. Query viewport dimensions from g_dwScreenWidth, g_dwScreenHeight
14. Query panel format with Ordinal_10638(gameMode, quality, format)
15. For each slot in viewport (count from local_104):
    - Get unit pointer via Ordinal_10271(gameHandle, index)
    - Validate unit with Ordinal_10707, Ordinal_10771, FUN_6fb6e180
    - If special monster (pdwCurrentUnit match), use alternate palette
    - Render panel with FUN_6fb92980 and unit data with FUN_6fb91bf0
    - If unit keybindable, lookup keybinding with LookupKeyBindingByCommandId
    - Format and display key binding string in local_1d0 (Unicode)
16. Check if special monster selected (g_dwSelectedMonsterIndex >= 0)
17. If selected and visible, fetch with Ordinal_10271
18. Validate special monster with Ordinal_10768
19. Render special monster with alternate palette

Parameters:
   None - void function, reads global game state

Returns:
   None - void function

Special Cases:
   Game mode validation: Validates mode between 0-5 with switch statement
   Palette colors: Uses Ordinal_10034 to create 8-bit palette entries from 24-bit RGB
   Key binding truncation: Limits Unicode string to 0x1c (28) characters
   Monster selection: Special rendering for g_dwSelectedMonsterIndex if >= 0
   Stack arrays: Local arrays use 0x250 (592 bytes) of local stack space

Magic Numbers:
   0x84 - Game status structure unit handle offset
   0x8 - Slot validation parameter for Ordinal_10257
   0x13 - Expected unit type value from Ordinal_10751
   0x1f - Input state check code
   0x9 - Game state flag check code
   0x2 - Game mode for inactive state
   0x80 - RGB component value (128 decimal) for palette
   0x5 - Maximum game mode value
   0x12 - Panel data array element count (18)
   0x20 - Y-offset increment per panel (32 pixels)
   0x1c - Max key binding string length (28 chars)
   0x1d - Panel display width/height (29 pixels)
   0x29 - Y-offset base value
   0x250 - Total stack frame size (592 bytes)

functions.name: InitializeAndBuildItemTooltipDisplay
functions.comment:
Initialize and build item tooltip display buffers for game UI rendering.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize three Unicode character buffers (local_1fe: 256 elements, aUStack_5fe: 128 elements, aUStack_4fe: 384 elements)
2. Clear buffers with memset pattern and call Unicode default constructors on each element
3. Call LoadGameConfiguration to retrieve current game state
4. Check if game state (g_pCurrentGameState) and inventory (g_pCurrentInventory) are valid
5. If valid, retrieve owner inventory via Ordinal_10600 and validate item container exists
6. If validation fails, abort with fatal error (Ordinal_10023, FUN_6fb9a10f)
7. Load base item configuration and process formatting via ProcessUnicodeLineFormatting
8. Build item tooltip text via FUN_6fb5a3a0 for both 3-part and base configurations
9. Concatenate strings using Unicode::strcpy and Unicode::strcat
10. If item slot (g_nSelectedItemSlot) and display window (g_hDisplayWindow) are valid (>= 0):
    a. Prepare tooltip information via FUN_6fb5a350
    b. Validate object type via IsObjectTypeValid
    c. If valid, build item description via BuildItemTooltipText
    d. If description generated (dwResult != 0 && sDescLength != 0), concatenate additional strings
11. Request display update via Ordinal_10129

Parameters:
None (uses global variables: g_pCurrentGameState, g_pCurrentInventory, g_dwGameState, g_dwInventoryFlags, g_dwMinItemLevel, g_nSelectedItemSlot, g_hDisplayWindow, unaff_EDI, unaff_ESI)

Returns:
None (void function)

Special Cases:
- Function allocates large stack buffers (total 2096 bytes for Unicode arrays)
- Unaffected registers (unaff_EDI, unaff_ESI) indicate register parameters passed implicitly
- Uses D2Common Ordinal calls for game object validation and synchronization
- String operations use Unicode library functions (strcpy, strcat)

Magic Numbers:
0x7f - Loop counter for 256 Unicode element initialization (size check: 0x7f + 1 = 0x80 = 128 UTF-16 units = 256 bytes)
0xff - Second loop counter for 256 elements (0xff + 1 = 0x100 = 256 elements)
0x3f - Loop counter for 128 elements (0x3f + 1 = 0x40 = 64 UTF-16 units = 128 bytes)
0x7f - Loop counter for 128 elements
0xbf - Loop counter for 384 elements (0xbf + 1 = 0xc0 = 192 UTF-16 units = 384 bytes)
0x17f - Loop counter for 384 elements (0x17f + 1 = 0x180 = 384 elements)
0x84 - Offset into game state for player inventory pointer
0x1f - Loop counter for 64 elements (0x1f + 1 = 0x20 = 32 UTF-16 units = 64 bytes)
0x3f - Loop counter for 64 elements
0x200 - Formatting code for ProcessUnicodeLineFormatting
0x40 - Max description length for BuildItemTooltipText
1 - Format parameter for BuildItemTooltipText (item details format)

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
  -0x1fe | 512  | local_1fe | ushort[256] | Main tooltip text buffer (UTF-16 Unicode)
  -0x200 | 2    | sTooltipCount | short | Tooltip state counter
  -0x5fe | 508  | aUStack_5fe | ushort[254] | Secondary format buffer
  -0x600 | 2    | sItemLength | short | Item name/stat length
  -0x4fe | 1532 | aUStack_4fe | ushort[766] | Extended description buffer
  [stack] | 4   | dwResult | uint | BuildItemTooltipText result
  [stack] | 4   | iLoopCount | int | Loop counter (optimization reused)

functions.name: UpdateScreenAnimationTimer
functions.comment:
Updates the screen animation timer by retrieving current animation ID and resetting counter.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve current animation ID via FUN_6fb634e0()
2. If animation ID is valid (non-zero):
   a. Translate animation ID via Ordinal_10057 (D2Common ordinal)
   b. Compare with previously stored animation ID (g_dwCurrentScreenAnimId)
   c. If different, reset counter to 0x3c (60 decimal) and store new ID
3. Return

Parameters:
(none)

Returns:
(void) - updates globals g_dwCurrentScreenAnimId and g_dwScreenAnimUpdateCounter

Special Cases:
- If FUN_6fb634e0() returns 0 (no animation), function exits without updating globals
- Magic number 0x3c = 60 decimal (likely animation frame reset counter)

Related Functions:
- FUN_6fb634e0() - Retrieves current animation ID
- Ordinal_10057 - D2Common animation ID translator
- RenderMainGameScreen() - Caller, main render loop

functions.name: HandleMinimapButtonClick
functions.comment:
Handle minimap/panel button click detection and triggering.

Algorithm:
1. Get current mouse coordinates via FUN_6fb8f680 (X) and FUN_6fb8f690 (Y)
2. Calculate button region bounds: center screen ±8 pixels X, bottom area (height-0x27 to height-0x0d) Y
3. Check if mouse is within button click region
4. If within bounds, call FUN_6fb5d340(0x15) to check button state (0x15 likely button ID)
5. If button active (non-zero return), call Ordinal_10004 with Y offset -0x27, then Ordinal_10129
6. If button inactive (zero return), skip step 5 calls
7. Both paths push dwMode1=0 and dwMode2=1 as parameters before conditional calls

Parameters:
None - reads screen state from global variables

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Button region: screen center X ±8 pixels (-8 to +5), screen height-0x27 to height-0x0d Y
- Magic values: 0x15 (button ID), 0x27 (button Y offset), 0x0d (button height offset)
- Two ordinal calls (10004, 10129) likely handle button rendering/state update

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x15: Button ID (likely minimap expand/collapse)
- 0x27: Y offset for button bottom edge (39 pixels from screen height)
- 0x0d: Button height adjustment (13 pixels)
- 0x08, 0x05: X bounds tolerance (±8/-5 pixels from center)

functions.name: ValidateViewportPosition
functions.comment:
Validates and adjusts viewport position to stay within screen boundaries.

Algorithm:
1. Check IsGameSystemEnabled - if enabled, mark processed and return
2. Validate viewport via FUN_6fb62890 - if invalid, return early
3. Extract X (bits 0-15) and Y (bits 16-31) from element offset 0x0c
4. Call FUN_6fb300a0 to validate bounds - if failed, set update flag and return
5. If Y exceeds screen_height - 0x30, mark processed and return
6. Check if X or Y violates screen boundaries (X < 0x75, X != 0xa5, Y > screen_height)
7. Adjust position based on screen region: center, left/right, or bottom
8. Set UI update flag and call Ordinal_511 to trigger viewport refresh

Parameters:
pUIElement - UIObject pointer; position coords at offset 0x0c, flags at 0x18-0x1c

Returns:
void - Updates element position in-place; sets global UI state flags

Special Cases:
Early return if game disabled or viewport invalid; handles coordinates outside visible screen area

functions.name: ValidateViewportAndSendPacket
functions.signature: void ValidateViewportAndSendPacket(dword dwGameMode, dword dwGraphicsMode, int nX, int nY)
functions.comment:
Validates viewport coordinates against game bounds and sends packet with position or visibility data.

Algorithm:
1. Call Ordinal_10638 to fetch viewport bounds into local_108
2. Check if slot count (local_104) is zero - exit if empty
3. Loop through up to N slots: Call Ordinal_10639 with each index
4. Validate coordinates: param_3 (X) and param_4 (Y) must be within [min,max] bounds
5. When valid slot found, retrieve both new and previous unit pointers via Ordinal_10262 and Ordinal_10271
6. Validate game mode (FUN_6fb8f780 != 6)
7. Check unit existence and validity (Ordinal_10768)
8. Send packet: type 0x24 (only previous), 0x23 (only new), or 0x25 (both)
9. Call FUN_6fb6bc10 to get rendering context, update camera/viewport with FUN_6fb8d210

Parameters:
  dwGameMode (ECX): Game mode identifier
  dwGraphicsMode (EDX): Graphics quality flag
  nX: Viewport X coordinate to validate
  nY: Viewport Y coordinate to validate

Returns: void

Special Cases:
  - If no valid slot exists (all iterations exhausted), returns early
  - If coordinate validation fails for all slots, returns early
  - If game mode is 0x6, returns early
  - uVar4 & 0xffff masks Y coordinate to 16-bit value for packet
  - FUN_6fb6e180 return value indicates unit validity

Magic Numbers:
  0x24: Packet type for previous-only visibility
  0x23: Packet type for new-only visibility
  0x25: Packet type for both units visible
  0x6: Game mode check (disable condition)
  0xffff: Y coordinate mask to 16 bits
  0x8: Field offset for unit data values (puVar1[2], puVar2[2])

Related Functions:
  - Ordinal_10638: Fetch viewport bounds
  - Ordinal_10639: Iterate viewport slots
  - Ordinal_10262: Get previous unit pointer
  - Ordinal_10271: Get new unit pointer by index
  - FUN_6fb8f780: Get game mode status
  - FUN_6fb6e180: Validate unit structure
  - FUN_6fb6e120: Cleanup unit reference
  - FUN_6fb6bc10: Get rendering/camera context
  - FUN_6fb8d210: Update viewport camera position

functions.name: HandleViewportClick
functions.signature: void HandleViewportClick(dword dwGameMode, dword dwUnitIndex, int nClickX, int nClickY)
functions.comment:
Processes viewport click events to select units/monsters in the current game view.

Algorithm:
1. Query renderer for current viewport slot boundaries (Ordinal_10638)
2. Iterate through available slots checking if click coordinates fall within slot bounds
3. For matching slot: retrieve unit/monster data via ordinal calls
4. Validate game state (not in skill/quest dialogs via FUN_6fb8f780)
5. If unit found: store as selected unit, update global selection state
6. Else if no unit: clear selection and set monster visibility flags

Parameters:
  dwGameMode (ECX): Game mode/graphics quality identifier
  dwUnitIndex (EDX): Unit/monster index in current context
  nClickX (Stack+0x4): X coordinate of viewport click (1-based)
  nClickY (Stack+0x8): Y coordinate of viewport click (1-based)

Returns:
  void: Updates global selection state (g_pSelectedUnitData, g_dwSelectedMonsterIndex, etc)

Special Cases:
  - If slot count is 0 (bySlotCount=0): Function exits immediately
  - If no slot found within bounds: Returns without changing selection
  - If game state is 6 or 8 (skill/quest dialogs): Function returns without selection
  
Magic Numbers:
  0x80, 0xff: Slot count bit mask for valid slots
  0x0e: Offset added to slot minimum for item slot calculation
  0x6: Game state indicating skill dialog active
  0x8: Game state indicating quest dialog active

Global Data Modified:
  g_pSelectedUnitData (0x6fbf9034): Pointer to selected unit
  g_dwSelectedMonsterIndex (0x6fbb7550): Index of selected monster
  g_dwMonsterVisible (0x6fbf901c): Monster visibility flag
  g_pdwCurrentUnit (0x6fbf9030): Pointer to current unit
  g_nSelectedItemSlot (0x6fbb7554): Selected slot index + 0x0e
  g_hDisplayWindow (0x6fbb7558): Display window handle

functions.name: ProcessPlayerItemState
functions.signature: void ProcessPlayerItemState(int nPlayerId, dword dwItemUnitType, dword dwItemId)
functions.comment:
Validates and processes player item state for slot management with renderer initialization

Algorithm:
1. Check if item type is already allocated via Ordinal_10262 - if so, return early
2. Call FUN_6fb5d340 to check memory availability (param 9)
3. Get system state via GetGlobalSystemState
4. Query item unit pointer via Ordinal_10409 and apply graphics quality flag via Ordinal_10636 to local_18 buffer
5. Retrieve item unit data via Ordinal_10271(itemType, itemId) - store in pItemUnitData
6. If item unit exists:
   a. Validate item stat exists via Ordinal_10600(itemStat[1]) - log critical error and terminate via FUN_6fb9a10f if NULL
   b. Check equippable flags at offsets 0x29 and 0x2a - if set, process equip action via FUN_6fb58e40 and return
   c. Check identify flag at offset 0x25 - if NOT set, send error (0x13) via FUN_6fb88d60 and return
   d. Get item renderer state via FUN_6fb6e180 - if already initialized, skip processing
   e. Initialize new renderer:
      - Get player stat ID via Ordinal_10329(playerIndex)
      - Get player unit ID via Ordinal_10326(playerIndex)
      - Send network packet type 0x26 with item data via SendPacketWithSubcommand
      - Clean up existing renderer via FUN_6fb6e120
      - Initialize flCoordX and flY to 0.0 (coordinate placeholders)
      - Query monster visibility data via FUN_6fb6bc60
      - Process item rendering via FUN_6fb8d210 with zero coordinates
      - Clear global monster visibility flag (g_dwMonsterVisible = 0)

Parameters:
  nPlayerId (int, IMPLICIT ECX) - Player unit index in active roster, used for stat/ID queries
  dwItemType (dword, IMPLICIT EDX) - Item type enumeration from D2Common item table
  dwItemId (dword, stack at +0x4) - Item instance ID from unit memory system

Returns: void (all paths return without value)

Special Cases:
- Critical item stat missing: logs error details and terminates process via FUN_6fb9a10f(0xFFFFFFFF)
- No system memory available (FUN_6fb5d340 check fails): early return without processing
- Item type already initialized (Ordinal_10262 returns non-zero): early return without processing
- Invalid item flags (offset 0x25 not set): error code 0x13 sent via FUN_6fb88d60, return early
- Renderer already initialized (FUN_6fb6e180 returns non-zero): skip initialization, return early
- Equippable item (flags 0x29 or 0x2a set): special equip processing via FUN_6fb58e40, return early

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x29, 0x2a - Equippable/usable item flag offsets in D2Common.UnitAny structure (byte-sized flags, 0x01 = true)
  0x25 - Identify flag offset in item unit structure (0x01 = identified item, required for processing)
  0x26 - Network packet subcommand type for item state update packet
  0x13 - Error code for invalid item state, passed to FUN_6fb88d60
  0x4 - Stack cleanup on return (RET 0x4 - remove 4-byte parameter from stack)
  0x18 - Local stack allocation (24 bytes for graphics buffer)

functions.name: SetGameStateByteFlag
functions.comment:
Set a game state flag byte at the specified index.

Algorithm:
1. Compare dwIndex against 0x4 boundary (size check)
2. If dwIndex < 0x4, store byValue into g_abGameStateFlags[dwIndex]
3. Return (early exit if dwIndex >= 0x4)

Parameters:
  dwIndex (uint, ECX): Array index, must be in range [0, 4)
  byValue (byte, DL): Flag value to store

Returns:
  void (no return value)

Special Cases:
  - If dwIndex >= 0x4, array access is prevented (bounds check)
  - Flag can be any byte value (0x00-0xFF)

Array Layout:
  Base Address: g_abGameStateFlags (0x6fbf9038)
  Element Size: 1 byte
  Max Index: 3 (0-3, 4 elements total)

functions.name: InitializeGameStateFlags
functions.comment:
Initialize game state flags to cleared/unselected values

Algorithm:
1. Set g_dwSelectedMonsterIndex to 0xFFFFFFFF (no monster selected)
2. Set g_nSelectedItemSlot to 0xFFFFFFFF (no item slot selected)
3. Set g_hDisplayWindow to 0xFFFFFFFF (no window handle)
4. Set g_dwMonsterVisible to 0x00000000 (visibility cleared)
5. Set g_pdwCurrentUnit to NULL (no current unit)
6. Set g_pSelectedUnitData to NULL (no selected unit data)

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- 0xFFFFFFFF marker indicates "uninitialized/not-selected" state for indices/handles
- NULL pointers used for pointer-type globals
- Called during game initialization to reset UI/gameplay state

functions.name: ValidateCoordinateInBounds
functions.comment:
Validate if screen coordinates are within active game or UI bounds.

Algorithm:
1. Extract X coordinate (lower 16-bit) and Y coordinate (upper 16-bit) from coordinate pointer + 0xc
2. Call Ordinal_10638 with game mode and graphics quality flags to prepare render data
3. Check if game is active (g_dwGameActive == 0 indicates menu/UI screen)
   - If INACTIVE: Validate coordinates against menu UI bounds (hardcoded offsets)
     - Min X: g_dwScreenWidth/2 + 0x17, Max X: g_dwScreenWidth/2 + 0x91
     - Min Y: g_dwScreenHeight - 0x30, Max Y: g_dwScreenHeight - 0x27
   - If ACTIVE: Validate against game UI panel bounds
     - Panel index = (dwMode & 0xff) - 4 
     - Bounds loaded from aiStack_100 array: [MinX, unused, MinY, MaxY]
     - X: aiStack_100[index*4] <= X <= local_cc
     - Y: aiStack_100[index*4+2] <= Y <= local_c4
4. Return 1 if coordinates within bounds, 0 otherwise

Parameters:
- nCoordPtr (int, __fastcall ECX): Pointer to coordinate structure (X at +0xc offset as packed shorts)

Returns:
- 1: Coordinates are within valid bounds
- 0: Coordinates are outside bounds

Special Cases:
- Coordinate encoding: X in lower 16-bit, Y in upper 16-bit of 32-bit value
- Menu bounds use hardcoded offsets relative to screen dimensions
- Game bounds array index calculated as (mode & 0xFF) - 4 for up to 13 panels

functions.name: InitializeUnitState
functions.comment:
Initialize unit state by clearing global unit pointers

Algorithm:
1. Load 0 into EAX register
2. Store 0 to g_pdwCurrentUnit global
3. Store 0 to g_pSelectedUnitData global
4. Return to caller

Parameters:
(none)

Returns:
void (no return value)

Special Cases:
Called during initialization phase to establish clean state

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x6fbf9030 - Address of g_pdwCurrentUnit global variable
0x6fbf9034 - Address of g_pSelectedUnitData global variable

Related Functions:
- FUN_6fb5da20() - Initialization routine that calls this function

functions.name: SetGameActive
functions.comment:
Set the game active flag to 1.

Algorithm:
1. Write 1 to the global flag g_dwGameActive at address 0x6fbf9020

Parameters:
void

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
Called conditionally when DAT_6fbfd7d8 flag is set during game state rendering

functions.name: InitializeRandomSeed
functions.comment:
Initialize random seed generator with entropy parameters

Algorithm:
1. Call Ordinal_10034 (D2Common.RandSeed) with entropy values (0xff, 0, 0)
2. Store result in global g_bRandomSeedInitialized

Parameters:
None - void function

Returns:
byte - Result from RandSeed call (typically 1 on success, 0 on failure)

functions.name: InitializeGameViewportConfig
functions.comment:
Initialize game viewport configuration state by invoking Storm.dll function.

Algorithm:
1. Push three zero parameters (context flags, reserved, flags) onto stack
2. Call Ordinal_10034 (Storm.GetDisplayMode - retrieves display configuration)
3. Store AL register result (display mode byte) to global g_byViewportConfigState
4. Return to caller

Parameters:
None (void function)

Returns:
void - Updates g_byViewportConfigState with display mode configuration from Storm.dll

Special Cases:
Function always called before viewport rendering initialization (InitializeViewportRendering).
Result stored as single byte despite EAX return value (upper 3 bytes discarded).
Zero parameters to Storm.GetDisplayMode indicate query-only operation (no flags set).

Related Functions:
- InitializeViewportRendering() - Caller; uses this function to initialize display state first
- RenderPlayerStatisticsOverlay() - References g_byViewportConfigState indirectly via rendering logic
- Ordinal_10034() - Storm.dll display mode query function (3 parameters: reserved, reserved, flags)

functions.name: ProcessLinkedListNodes
functions.comment:
Traverse and process linked list nodes, calling Ordinal_10043 for each entry.

Algorithm:
1. Load linked list head pointer from g_pLinkedListHead
2. If list is empty (NULL), zero the global and return
3. Loop: Get next node pointer from current node at offset 0xcd
4. Call Ordinal_10043(0x107, 0) for processing each node
5. Continue until next pointer is NULL
6. Store final pointer value to g_pLinkedListHead and return

Parameters:
(none)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Empty list: Returns immediately after zeroing g_pLinkedListHead
- List structure: Next pointer at offset 0xcd (205 bytes from node start)

functions.name: BuildPlayerSlotList
functions.comment:
Constructs linked list of player slot structures. Iterates through player roster, allocates memory for each slot, initializes slot data with player attributes and configuration values.

Algorithm:
1. Clear existing linked list (walk through g_pLinkedListHead chain, deallocate each node)
2. Initialize cursor base offset to 0x5a, get first player roster entry
3. Loop through player roster:
   - Return if end of roster and player count >= 9
   - Allocate 0x14c bytes for new slot structure (via Ordinal_10042)
   - Zero initialize allocated buffer (52 dwords + 1 byte)
   - Set slot structure header fields (ID, type flags, base offset)
   - Query player slot status checks (access privilege, board status, slot status)
   - Set slot structure status fields based on privilege checks (result & 0x2 + base value)
   - Copy player roster name to slot structure (src GetRosterFieldAt0x66, dst puVar7+0xa0)
   - Set player unit type and field data (unit type, field 0x20, field 0x24)
   - Insert new slot structure into linked list tail
   - Increment cursor base offset by 0x26, advance to next roster entry

Parameters:
  (void) - Operates on globals: g_pLinkedListHead (linked list head), roster entry state

Returns:
  void - Modifies global player slot list structure

Magic Numbers:
  0x5a - Initial slot cursor offset value
  0x14c - Size of allocated slot structure buffer
  0x34 - Count of dwords to zero (slot structure initialization)
  0x107, 0x14c - Ordinal parameters (memory management calls)
  0xcd - Offset within slot/node structure for linked list pointer
  0xc9 - Offset for cursor position within slot structure
  0xa0 - Offset for player name buffer within slot structure

functions.name: RenderCharacterCreateScreen
functions.comment:
Render the character creation screen with UI frames and player slot information.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize 4 UI frame positions for character selection class display (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right)
2. Retrieve current player character data via GetPlayerTargetDataByInfo()
3. If player name exists, convert to Unicode and display centered at top (max width 0xb)
4. Initialize linked list head for player slots
5. For each of 8 player slots: fetch node, validate player ID with CheckPlayerIdDuplicate()
   a. Compare current vs first player ID to detect duplicates (sets status code 0x2)
   b. Check unit identifiers with CompareUnitIdentifiers() for conflicts (status 0x1)
   c. Set status 0x8 for normal valid slots
   d. Render frame data, field indicators, skills with FUN_6fb309e0/FUN_6fb30b10/FUN_6fb308f0
   e. If duplicate flag set and slot has special flag, render extra data via FUN_6fb30e00
   f. Advance to next player slot in linked list
6. Display "SELECT" button frame at bottom right (position 0x116, 0x1a5)
7. If button clicked via FUN_6fb31020(), render zoom animation with Ordinal_10129()

Parameters:
None (uses global UI state and player slot data via GetPlayerNodeNext, GetPlayerTargetDataByInfo)

Returns:
None (renders to screen)

Special Cases:
- First player ID (-1) skipped in loop, slots 2-9 processed
- Character name truncated if wider than 0xb (width 0xc triggers Ordinal_10127)
- Button click triggers animation parameters: Y offset 0x182 (adjusted for UI offset)
- Hardcore mode flag (g_bHardcoreFlagEnabled) affects secondary frame display

functions.name: GetUnitInventoryForUI
functions.signature: void GetUnitInventoryForUI(dword dwUnitId, int nScreenX, int nScreenY, dword dwColor)
functions.comment:
Display unit inventory at screen coordinates with color key.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize 18-element DWORD buffer (adwItemBuffer) on stack to zero
   - Use EDI pointer arithmetic and REP STOSD for efficient zeroing
   - Clears 0x12 (18) elements = 72 bytes total
2. Set buffer[3] = 0 (terminator/padding field)
3. Set buffer[2] = dwColor (color override key passed to renderer)
4. Set buffer[1] = dwUnitId (unit identifier/reference)
5. Retrieve X offset from global g_dwUIXOffset
6. Retrieve Y offset from global g_dwUIYOffset
7. Call D2Common.GetUnitInventory (Ordinal_10072) with:
   - Buffer address (pointer to adwItemBuffer)
   - Adjusted X = g_dwUIXOffset + nScreenX
   - Adjusted Y = nScreenY - g_dwUIYOffset
   - Color key 0xffffffff (no override)
   - Priority 5 (standard UI layer)
   - Flags 0 (default behavior)
8. Inventory items rendered by callee, function returns immediately

Parameters:
dwUnitId (dword): Unit ID/entity pointer in ECX register
nScreenX (int): Viewport X coordinate in EDX register
nScreenY (int): Viewport Y coordinate on stack [ESP+0x58]
dwColor (dword): Color key for rendering on stack [ESP+0x54]

Returns:
void - All work delegated to D2Common.GetUnitInventory ordinal call
Inventory structure populated in-place and rendered by callee

Special Cases:
Buffer layout: 18 DWORDs (72 bytes) for inventory item display
Magic numbers: 0x12 = 18 items, 0xffffffff = no color override, 5 = UI priority
Screen coordinate adjustment required due to viewport offset globals

functions.name: BuildUILabelString
functions.signature: void BuildUILabelString(dword dwLabelId, dword dwYOffset, dword dwWidgetId)
functions.comment:
Constructs a formatted UI label string and displays it on the interface at specified coordinates.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize 100 Unicode characters in stack buffer at [ESP + 0x24]
2. Initialize 10 Unicode characters in stack buffer at [ESP + 0x10]
3. Call Ordinal_10004 (UI resource lock/reference)
4. Call strncpy to copy label text to destination
5. Call Ordinal_10004 twice to format and concatenate strings
6. Call wsprintfA to format dwLabelId as decimal string using format string g_szFormatPercent
7. Call win2Unicode to convert formatted ANSI string to Unicode (max 9 chars)
8. Call strcat to concatenate Unicode string to display buffer
9. Call Ordinal_10117 (D2UI.TakeScreenCoord) with adjusted Y coordinate (dwYOffset - g_dwUIYOffset) and widget ID
10. Call display function through ESI to render label on screen

Parameters:
- dwLabelId (uint, ECX): Label resource ID to format and display
- dwYOffset (int, EDX): Y coordinate offset for label placement
- dwWidgetId (uint, Stack[0x4]): Widget identifier for the UI control

Returns:
- None (void)

Special Cases:
- Magic number 0x140 (320 bytes) is total stack allocation for three buffers
- Unicode buffers: 200 chars (0x18c bytes) + 20 chars (0x28 bytes)
- ANSI buffer: 100 chars (0x64 bytes)
- Y coordinate is offset by g_dwUIYOffset, indicating screen coordinate system correction
- The function performs UI coordinate transformation before calling display routine

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x140 (320): Total stack allocation size
- 0x64 (100): ANSI formatting buffer size in characters
- 100: Count of Unicode characters to initialize (200-byte buffer = 100 wide chars)
- 10: Count of Unicode characters for temporary buffer (20-byte buffer = 10 wide chars)
- 0x9 (9): Maximum characters for number formatting
- 0x10a (266): UI coordinate offset constant
- 0x14 (20): Lock/reference count for ordinal call
- 0xd28, 0xf9d, 0xf9b: Internal ordinal parameters

Related Functions:
- Ordinal_10004 (UI resource management)
- Ordinal_10117 (D2UI screen coordinate handling)
- wsprintfA (ANSI string formatting)
- Unicode string operations (initialization, copying, concatenation)

functions.name: ProcessUnicodeStringWithFilter
functions.signature: void ProcessUnicodeStringWithFilter(char * szInput, int nMaxLen, int nOutputLen, int nHighFilter)
functions.comment:
Processes input Unicode string with character filtering based on mode

Algorithm:
1. Initialize 98-character Unicode buffer (aUnicodeBuffer) with constructor calls
2. Convert input string szInput to Unicode in buffer (toUnicode call, max 100 chars)
3. Initialize 5-character temp buffer (aUStack_d8) with constructors
4. Load config value from g_szEllipsisString into dwConfig
5. Branch on nHighFilter: if zero, use threshold 0x88; else use 0x60
6. Call Ordinal_10121 (character generation) repeatedly
7. Filter loop: while character > threshold, move backward and write 0x0000 (null wide char)
8. Convert config bytes to Unicode (5 chars max)
9. Concatenate temp buffer to output using strcat (unaff_EDI, unaff_ESI from caller)
10. Calculate final Y offset by subtracting g_dwUIYOffset and decrementing by 2
11. Call Ordinal_10117 (output rendering) with offset, length, and zero flag

Parameters:
szInput (char *) - IMPLICIT ECX: pointer to source ANSI string to convert
nMaxLen (int) - IMPLICIT EDX: maximum length for buffer (100 chars)
nOutputLen (int) - Stack[4]: length parameter for output operation
