- FUN_6fb5e930 - Check for animation update trigger

functions.name: InitializeAlwaysRunSetting
functions.comment:
Initialize the Always Run game setting from configuration file.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize local buffer variable to zero
2. Call Ordinal_423 (likely D2Common.GetConfigVariable) to read 'Always Run' setting from Diablo II configuration
3. Pass configuration value to SetAlwaysRunFlag to apply setting

Parameters:
None - reads global configuration and applies to game state

Returns:
void - no return value

Special Cases:
Function is called during game UI initialization sequence. Sets game behavior flag that persists during session.

functions.name: SaveAlwaysRunSetting
functions.comment:
Retrieve and save the "Always Run" gameplay setting to config.

Algorithm:
1. Get the current "Always Run" setting value via GetAlwaysRunSetting()
2. Call Ordinal_426 to save setting (assumed config write function)
   - Parameters: product name (g_szDiabloII), key name (szAlwaysRunKey), reserved (0), setting value
3. Return

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
None

Related Functions:
- GetAlwaysRunSetting() - Retrieves current "Always Run" setting value
- Ordinal_426() - Config/registry write function (D2Common)

functions.name: UpdateGameUIState
functions.comment:
Update game UI state and render mode based on game state and mode flags
Validates multiple game state conditions and adjusts UI rendering modes accordingly

Algorithm:
1. Check all 14 core game state validity flags (checks performed via FUN_6fb5d340 with various state indices)
2. If all core state flags pass (return 0), set g_fGameStateInitialCheckFailed = 0
3. Otherwise, set flag = 1 indicating state validation failure
4. Check additional state flag 0x24; if set, mark g_fGameStateInitialCheckFailed = 1
5. Validate secondary state flags (different indices); if any set (non-zero), set g_fGameModeWarningActive = 1
6. Check flag 0x1f; if set OR game state inactive (IsGameStateActive), mark warning active
7. Check game mode via GetGameModeFlag; if mode > 1, mark warning active
8. Check flags 1 and 4; if both clear (zero), clear g_fGameModeWarningActive; otherwise set to 1
9. Branch logic:
   - If fGameStateCheckFailed AND fGameModeWarning: disable all UI panels (call Update functions with 0), set render mode = 1
   - If fGameStateCheckFailed only: initialize UI buffer, place window at calculated screen position, disable panel 3, render button array, set render mode = 0
   - If fGameModeWarning only: disable all panels (call functions with 1), set render mode = 0
   - If neither flag set: initialize UI buffer, place window at alternate position, disable panel 2, disable panel 1, set render mode = 0

Parameters:
(none)

Returns:
void - Updates global UI state flags and triggers UI rendering updates

Special Cases:
- Screen position calculations depend on g_fResolutionMode flag (normal vs expanded resolution)
- UI button array (g_aUIButtonArray) processed conditionally based on render mode
- Button iteration uses dynamic count (7 or 8) based on resolution mode
- Button offset calculation adds +1 if field [0x10] equals 1

Related Functions:
- FUN_6fb5d340 - Check game state flag
- IsGameStateActive - Query if game is active
- GetGameModeFlag - Get current game mode
- FUN_6fb377e0 - Update UI panel (call with 0, 1, or disable)
- FUN_6fb37910 - Update button panel
- FUN_6fb379f0 - Update text/help panel
- FUN_6fb37aa0 - Update status panel
- FUN_6fb378d0 - Render button at position

functions.name: RenderGameMessagePanel
functions.comment:
Render game message panel with specified type and position on screen.

Algorithm:
1. Check if nPanelType is 0 (early exit)
2. Initialize 18-element message buffer array to zero
3. Set buffer[1] to icon resource ID from g_dwMessagePanelIconId
4. Branch on nPanelType:
   - Type 1: Render left-aligned panel at (width/2 - 205, height - 47)
   - Type 2: Render centered panel at conditional x-position (width/2 - 84 or -74), y = height - 47
   - Type 3: Render right-aligned panel at conditional x-position (width/2 + 35 or +56), y = height - 47
5. Call Ordinal_10072 (Storm.DrawText) to render text in buffer at calculated position

Parameters:
nPanelType (int) - Message panel type: 0=hide, 1=left, 2=center, 3=right

Returns:
void - No return value; renders directly to screen

Special Cases:
- Type 0 returns early without rendering
- Type 2 and 3 check g_dwExtendedPanelMode flag to adjust x-offset by 10-15 pixels
- All non-zero types render at same y-coordinate (height - 47)
- Color hardcoded to 0xFFFFFFFF (white), font size 5 pixels

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x12 (18) - Message buffer element count
0x2F (47) - Y-offset from screen bottom
0xCD (205), 0x54 (84), 0x4A (74), 0x23 (35), 0x38 (56) - X-position offsets from center
0xFFFFFFFF - White text color (ARGB)
0x5 (5) - Font size in pixels

functions.name: RenderUIElement
functions.signature: void RenderUIElement(int nElementIndex, dword dwX, dword dwY)
functions.comment:
Render a game UI element at the specified screen coordinates.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize 72-byte (18 dword) buffer on stack
2. Set buffer[1] to UI element configuration table pointer
3. Set buffer[2] to element index nElementIndex
4. Call Ordinal_10072 (rendering function) with:
   - Buffer as first parameter (contains configuration)
   - X coordinate (dwX)
   - Y coordinate (dwY)
   - Color mask (0xFFFFFFFF = white)
   - Drawing mode (5)
   - Reserved flag (0)

Parameters:
nElementIndex (ECX) - Element table index to render
dwX (EDX) - Screen X coordinate for element placement
dwY (Stack+4) - Screen Y coordinate for element placement

Returns:
void - No return value, updates screen buffer via Ordinal_10072 call

Special Cases:
- Always uses 0xFFFFFFFF (white) color mask
- Drawing mode fixed at 5 (standard UI drawing)
- Buffer must be zeroed before configuration (REP STOSD)

functions.name: InitializePanelSlotPositions
functions.comment:
Initialize panel slot positions and related data based on screen dimensions and panel configuration.

Algorithm:
1. Read panel configuration flag from g_dwPanelConfig
2. Calculate number of slot rows: 8 rows if config=0, 7 rows if config!=0
3. Calculate base X position: screen_width/2 - offset, adjusted for panel type and config
   - Type 1: offset = 0xCA (left side)
   - Type 3 with config=0: offset = 0x23 (far right)
   - Type 3 with config!=0: offset = 0x39 (right)
   - Other: offset = 0x54 (right), or 0x4A if config!=0
4. Calculate base Y position: screen_height - 0x32
5. Initialize array headers g_aPanelSlotXPositions[0] and g_aPanelSlotYPositions[0] with base positions
6. For each slot row (1 to uRowCount-1):
   - Calculate X position: add 0x15 (21 pixels) per row to base X
   - Store in g_aPanelSlotXPositions[row] and g_aPanelSlotYPositions[row]
   - If config=0 (disabled): slot indices = row, slot values = row*2
   - If config!=0 (enabled): slot indices = accumulator + row, slot values = penalty + row*2
     - Penalty increases by 2 every 3 rows, accumulator increments once every 3 rows
   - Store calculated indices/values in g_aPanelSlotIndices and g_aPanelSlotValues

Parameters:
nPanelType (int, ECX) - Panel type identifier (0=default, 1=left variant, 3=right variant)

Returns:
void - Function modifies global arrays

Special Cases:
- If nPanelType=0, no initialization occurs (early return)
- Panel configuration affects both positioning and slot mapping
- Slot penalty system only applies when config!=0

functions.name: ProcessUISlotRenderQueue
functions.comment:
Process UI slot rendering queue with conditional initialization.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize maximum slot count (8 or 7) based on DAT_6fbfa1a0 flag
2. If slot count is zero, return early
3. For each available slot (iterate nMaxSlots times):
   - Check if slot is active (piVar3[-8] == 1)
   - If active: Initialize aRenderData1 with incremented slot index and global value
   - If inactive: Initialize aRenderData2 with current slot index and global value
   - Call Ordinal_10072 to render the buffer
   - Advance slot pointer by 4 bytes

Parameters:
- nSlotCount (ECX): Number of UI slots to process; if 0, function returns immediately
- Implicit globals: DAT_6fbfa1a0 (flag), DAT_6fbfa138 (slot array base), DAT_6fbfa18c (config value)

Returns:
- void

Special Cases:
- If nSlotCount is 0, function exits without processing
- Maximum slot count is reduced to 7 if DAT_6fbfa1a0 is non-zero
- Stack arrays are cleared before use (18 dwords each)

functions.name: ProcessPanelSlotMouseHit
functions.comment:
Process panel slot mouse hit detection and key binding display

Algorithm:
1. Get current mouse position (screen coordinates)
2. Adjust X coordinate based on button parameter (-0x76 for button 1, 0x77 for button 3)
3. Check if mouse is within right-side panel boundaries (Y: screen_height-0x45 to -0x2f, X: adjusted ± 0x59)
4. If resolution mode flag set (DAT_6fbfa1a0 != 0), slot count = 7, else 8
5. Iterate through panel slot array (g_aPanelSlots), checking each slot X position
6. If slot X in range [slot_x, slot_x+0x14):
   a. Get command ID from slot offset +0x10
   b. Clear 400-char Unicode buffer (local_190)
   c. Call Ordinal_10004 (unknown, likely preprocessing)
   d. Copy base string to destination
   e. If valid command ID (not 0x39):
      - Look up primary key binding (slot offset +0x8)
      - If key exists (wKeyCode != 0xffff):
        * Clear 60-char Unicode buffer (aUStack_1cc)
        * Get key binding string and format into buffer via Ordinal_10004
        * Concatenate formatted key string to destination
      - Look up secondary key binding
      - Same process as primary if key exists
   f. Trigger panel update via Ordinal_10129 (slot_offset-0x1a, 0, 1)

Parameters:
  nMouseButton (ECX): Mouse button identifier (0=left, 1=middle, 3=right); used to adjust X offset

Returns:
  void; updates UI panel display as side effect

Special Cases:
  - Button 0: no X offset adjustment
  - Button 1: offset -0x76 pixels
  - Button 3: offset +0x77 pixels
  - Other buttons: no special handling
  - 0x39 is sentinel command ID indicating no key binding display

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x54: X offset bounds lower (-84 decimal)
  0x59: X offset bounds upper (+89 decimal)
  0x45: Y coordinate bottom boundary (69 decimal)
  0x2f: Y coordinate top boundary (47 decimal)
  0x14: Slot width (20 decimal)
  0x1a: Offset adjustment for panel update (26 decimal)
  0x76: Button 1 X offset magnitude (118 decimal, negative)
  0x77: Button 3 X offset magnitude (119 decimal)
  0xffff: Invalid key code sentinel
  0x39: Invalid command ID sentinel
  0xc8: Unicode buffer size (200 elements)
  0x1e: Small key binding buffer size (30 elements)

functions.name: HandlePanelModeDispatcher
functions.comment:
Dispatches handler code based on panel mode index (0-7).

Algorithm:
1. Compare nPanelMode with 7 (bounds check)
2. If nPanelMode > 7, return immediately
3. Jump to handler via jump table at [nPanelMode * 4 + 0x6fb3808c]
4. Each handler (0-5) calls FUN_6fb5d340 with mode index to check availability
5. Based on result (0 = unavailable, non-zero = available), call FUN_6fb5d370 with appropriate status code (1=available, 2=unavailable)
6. Handler 6: Output debug string "Panel_quest_log_toggle", call InitializeGameMode(0)
7. Handler 7: Execute shutdown sequence - call FUN_6fb5d910, FUN_6fb5d9a0, InitializePanelMode, FUN_6fb5d9b0, FUN_6fb5d9c0

Parameters:
nPanelMode (ECX register) - dword: Panel mode identifier (0=panel0, 1=panel1, 2=panel2, 3=server, 4=panel4, 5=combined, 6=quest, 7=shutdown)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Mode 3 (server): Only executes if GetCurrentServerPort() returns non-zero
- Mode 5: First checks FUN_6fb5d340(0x1f), then FUN_6fb5d340(0x18) and returns after both checks
- All modes except 6 and 7 use same pattern: check availability via FUN_6fb5d340, then call FUN_6fb5d370 with status
- Note: Function uses 1 stack-allocated temporary (iVar2 result) optimized away by compiler

functions.name: InitializeUIElementState
functions.comment:
Initialize UI element panel state and clear element configuration.

Algorithm:
1. Call GetCurrentServerPort() to determine connection state
2. If port is 0 (no server), load minipanel_s config resource via FUN_6fb5a050()
3. If port is non-zero, load minipanel config resource via FUN_6fb5a050()
4. Store icon resource ID in g_dwMessagePanelIconId
5. Set g_dwExtendedPanelMode: 1 if port=0, 0 if port!=0
6. Load minipanelbtn config resource via FUN_6fb5a050()
7. Store button resource ID in g_pUIElementConfigTable
8. Set nElementCount to 8 if extended mode, else 7
9. Iterate from nElementCount to 0, clearing g_adwUIElementState array
10. Return

Parameters:
(none)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- If nElementCount <= 0, array clearing loop skipped
- Uses REP STOSD for bulk zero initialization

Magic Numbers:
0x0 - No server port (connection inactive)
0x7 - Element count for normal mode
0x8 - Element count for extended mode

functions.name: CleanupUIElementsAndSlots
functions.comment:
Cleanup UI elements and slot configuration on shutdown or reset.

Algorithm:
1. Load mini-panel active flag from g_dwMiniPanelActive
2. Call Ordinal_426 (Storm log operation) with mini-panel string, flag set to 1, and panel state
3. Check if g_pUIElementList exists (non-null)
   - If present, report validation error and clear reference
4. Check if g_dwUISlotConfig exists (non-null)
   - If present, report validation error and clear reference
5. Return with cleanup complete

Parameters:
None (void function)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Only cleans up if UI elements or slot configs were previously allocated
- Uses conditional validation reporting to catch unexpected cleanup states
- g_dwMiniPanelActive flag determines mini-panel logging behavior

functions.name: IsCoordinateInAutomapBounds
functions.comment:
Check if screen coordinates fall within automap interaction bounds.

Algorithm:
1. Read global screen width (g_dwScreenWidth) and height (g_dwScreenHeight)
2. Calculate horizontal center: width / 2
3. Calculate left bound: center - 0x4a (74 pixels)
4. Calculate right bound: center + 0x47 (71 pixels)
5. Calculate top bound: height - 0x45 (69 pixels)
6. Calculate bottom bound: height - 0x32 (50 pixels)
7. Check if nX in range [left_bound, right_bound) AND nY in range (top_bound, bottom_bound)
8. Return 1 (true) if all conditions met, 0 (false) otherwise

Parameters:
- nX (ECX, dword): X-coordinate on screen
- nY (EDX, dword): Y-coordinate on screen

Returns:
- 1: Coordinates are within automap bounds
- 0: Coordinates are outside automap bounds

Special Cases:
- Bounds are asymmetric (74px left margin vs 71px right margin)
- Vertical bounds depend on screen height
- Used for click detection in automap UI window

functions.name: ReadResolutionAndConfigureGraphics
functions.comment:
Read resolution configuration from INI and configure graphics mode accordingly.

Algorithm:
1. Query resolution setting from Diablo II.ini using Ordinal_423 (Fog.dll - GetPrivateProfileIntA)
2. Initialize graphics mode to 0 (default)
3. If resolution value equals 1, set graphics mode to 2 (higher resolution)
4. Apply graphics mode configuration by calling SetGraphicsModeConfiguration

Parameters:
void - No parameters

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
Resolution value of 1 maps to graphics mode 2. Other values default to mode 0.

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x6fbae148 - Address of "Diablo II" string (INI section name)
0x6fbc5278 - Address of "Resolution" string (INI key name)
0x0 - Default value for GetPrivateProfileIntA if key not found
0x2 - Graphics mode value for resolution setting 1
0x1 - Resolution setting threshold value

functions.name: IsPointInUISlotRegion
functions.comment:
Checks if a mouse point is within an active UI inventory slot region

Algorithm:
1. Get current mouse X coordinate via FUN_6fb8f680
2. Get current mouse Y coordinate via FUN_6fb8f690
3. Check if item is in slot 0x14 (upper slot), abort if not present
4. Check if item is in slot 0x15 (lower slot), abort if not present
5. Calculate slot origin X based on g_dwUISlotExtendedFlag
   - If flag is clear: originX = (ScreenWidth / 2) + 0x23
   - If flag is set: originX = (ScreenWidth / 2) + 0x38
6. Determine slot width (column count) based on g_dwUISlotExtendedFlag
   - If flag is clear: width = 8 columns
   - If flag is set: width = 7 columns
7. Calculate slot height in pixels: height = width * 0x14 (20 pixels per column)
8. Calculate Y bounds: minY = ScreenHeight - 0x4c (332), maxY = ScreenHeight - 0x32 (366)
9. Validate point is within bounds:
   - X in range [originX, originX + height)
   - Y in range [minY, maxY)
10. Return 1 if point in region, else 0

Parameters:
(implicit) g_dwUISlotExtendedFlag - Flag controlling extended UI mode
(implicit) g_dwScreenWidth - Current screen width
(implicit) g_dwScreenHeight - Current screen height

Returns:
1 if mouse coordinates are within the slot region
0 if outside region or slot items not present

Special Cases:
- Returns immediately if either slot 0x14 or 0x15 is empty
- UI dimensions scale based on g_dwUISlotExtendedFlag (extended vs compact)
- Height calculation uses stride of 0x14 (20 decimal) pixels per column

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x14 (20 decimal) - Pixels per slot column (height stride)
0x23 (35 decimal) - Base X offset for compact UI mode
0x38 (56 decimal) - Base X offset for extended UI mode
0x4c (76 decimal) - Y offset subtracted from screen height (minY = height - 76)
0x32 (50 decimal) - Y offset subtracted from screen height (maxY = height - 50)

functions.name: ProcessViewportCollision
functions.signature: dword ProcessViewportCollision(int * pMinX, int * pMinY, int * pMaxX, int * pMaxY, int nItemWidth, int nItemHeight, int nMinX)
functions.comment:
Validates and adjusts a viewport rectangle against collision boundaries.

Algorithm:
1. Load screen height and calculate maximum Y coordinate (screen_height - 48)
2. Validate minimum X: if MinX < nMinX, adjust MaxX and set MinX to minimum threshold
3. Validate minimum Y: if MinY < 6, adjust MaxY and set MinY to 6
4. Validate maximum X: if MaxX >= nItemWidth, reduce MaxX and MinX by (MaxX - nItemWidth + 1)
5. Validate maximum Y: if MaxY >= screen_max_y, clamp MaxY to screen_max_y
6. Check collision rect count: if count > 31, raise assertion failure
7. Iterate collision rectangles: for each collision rect, test both X and Y bounds
8. X-bounds check: piVar6[2] >= MinX AND MaxX >= piVar6[0]
9. Y-bounds check: piVar6[3] >= MinY AND MaxY >= piVar6[1]
10. If both checks pass: adjust viewport based on nItemWidth and calculate final position
11. Return 0 on successful collision adjustment, return 1 if no collision detected

Parameters:
pMinX - Pointer to minimum X coordinate of viewport (adjusted in-place)
pMinY - Pointer to minimum Y coordinate of viewport (adjusted in-place)
pMaxX - Pointer to maximum X coordinate of viewport (adjusted in-place)
pMaxY - Pointer to maximum Y coordinate of viewport (adjusted in-place)
nItemWidth - Item width threshold for maximum X boundary
nItemHeight - Unused parameter (reserved for height threshold)
nMinX - Minimum X coordinate threshold for validation

Returns:
0 - Viewport successfully adjusted for collision
1 - No collision detected or viewport out of bounds

Magic Numbers:
0x30 (48) - Screen height offset
0x6 (6) - Minimum Y coordinate threshold
0x20 (32) - Collision rect count limit (assertion check at 31+)
0x48 (72) - Collision rect structure stride
0x120 (288) - Collision rect structure entry size in array

Structure Layout - Collision Rectangle (72 bytes):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x0    | 4    | left       | int  | Rect left boundary
0x4    | 4    | bottom     | int  | Rect bottom boundary
0x8    | 4    | right      | int  | Rect right boundary
0xc    | 4    | top        | int  | Rect top boundary
0x10   | 52   | reserved   | byte | Unused padding

Related Functions:
- FUN_6fb38640() - Calls this function
- Ordinal_10023() - Error handler for collision rect validation

functions.name: ProcessViewportUnits
functions.comment:
Process viewport units and build collision rect table for rendering.

Algorithm:
1. Get current center unit from game state (Ordinal_10010)
2. Get selected unit (FUN_6fb62880) and its data (Ordinal_10342)
3. Get viewport dimensions and resource context
4. Retrieve main unit from resource handle (GetValidatedResourceHandle)
5. Get viewport bounds (Ordinal_10035) - extract min Y and room count
6. For each room (0 to dwRoomCount): 
   a. Get first unit in room chain from room data
   b. Walk unit linked list (pUnit[0x43] = next unit)
   c. Check if unit visible: (flags & 0x80) != 0 AND type == 4 (monster)
   d. If visible and room count < 0x20: store unit in collision table
7. Calculate screen position based on center unit type:
   - If center unit: use viewport offset from GetRelativeViewportX/GetViewportYOffsetAdjusted
   - Otherwise: use Ordinal_10327/10330 for isometric coords, apply scroll window offset
8. For each valid unit, check if screen position within bounds
9. Build collision rectangle using FUN_6fb5a690 (get unit bounds)
10. Call ProcessViewportCollision up to 0xc times to resolve collisions
11. Store collision rect in arrays (left/bottom/right/top)
12. Determine unit color/palette based on type and flags (switch on Ordinal_10695)
13. Render collision rects via Ordinal_10132
14. Clear unit selection if no units processed (local_30 = 0)

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Color palette depends on unit type: demon (3), undead (2), boss (9), superunique (4), champion (8), other (5)
- Center unit displayed with selected color (5) if within viewport
- Non-center units use type-specific palette or flag-based colors (0x800/0x400000)
- Scroll window offset applied for split screen modes (modes 1-2)
- Collision checking limited to 0xc attempts per unit

Magic Numbers:
- 0x3b: Unit flags offset within unit structure
- 0x80: Unit visibility flag bit
- 0x2c: Room unit list pointer offset
- 0x43: Unit next pointer offset (in dwords)
- 0x48: Collision rect entry stride in arrays
- 0x20: Maximum collision rects
- 0x90: Unit data stride for rendering
- 0x40/0x80: Color palette selection flags
- 0xc: Max collision resolution attempts
- 0x2a: Character name offset in inventory
- 0x80 (at offset 0x80): Magic number check in inventory

Data Structures:
Units are processed from room data structures. Unit type 4 = monsters.
Collision rectangles stored in arrays with 0x48 byte stride:
  Offset | Size | Field          | Type     | Purpose
  0x0    | 4    | nLeft          | int      | Left edge screen X
  0x4    | 4    | nBottom        | int      | Bottom edge screen Y  
  0x8    | 4    | nRight         | int      | Right edge screen X
  0xc    | 4    | nTop           | int      | Top edge screen Y
  0x10.. | ...  | unitData       | byte[..] | Unit rendering data

functions.name: GetSkillStatOffset
functions.comment:
Calculate skill stat table offset based on skill ID and base offset.

Algorithm:
1. If skill ID < 0x9C (156): Calculate offset as nBaseOffset + (nSkillId * 4) + 0x27C7
   - Convert skill ID to offset using 4-byte stride
   - Check if battle net format initialized via Ordinal_10004 call
   - If format strings don't match (strcmp != 0), use 0x1115 offset
2. If skill ID in range 0xDD-0x118 (221-280): Return nBaseOffset + (nSkillId * 4) + 0x52A2
3. If skill ID in range 0xD9-0xDC (217-220): Return nBaseOffset + (nSkillId * 4) + 0x1021
4. Default: Return 0x1115

Parameters:
nSkillId: Skill ID value (0-0x118)
nBaseOffset: Base offset for calculation (usually loaded from game state)

Returns:
Calculated stat offset for skill properties lookup

functions.name: FormatLocalizationString
functions.signature: dword FormatLocalizationString(dword nIndex, int nParam2, int nParam3, int nParam4, int nParam5)
functions.comment:
Format and concatenate localized Unicode strings for display.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize Unicode string buffer (64 elements, 2 bytes each = 128 bytes)
2. Read formatting parameters from structure at param_3 (offsets 0xe0, 0xe4, 0xdc)
3. If both params at 0xe0 and 0xe4 are zero, return 0 (invalid/empty)
4. If param_5 is non-zero (alternate format mode):
   - Call Ordinal_10004 four times (initialization sequence)
   - Initialize 16-element Unicode buffer
   - Call Ordinal_578 with format string and param_5
   - Convert result from ANSI to Unicode
   - Append to output string via strcat (EDI register) 4 times
5. Else (standard format mode):
   - Calculate value: dwValue = ((param_4 - 1) * param_3[0xe4] + param_3[0xe0]) << shift
   - If param_2 == 6: clamp dwValue to 0 if negative
   - Else: clamp dwValue to minimum 0x100
   - If depth=8 OR param_3[0xe4]<<shift > 0x100 OR dwValue > 0xc00 (large format):
     a. Calculate high nibble: iHigh = dwValue >> 8
     b. Format to string using g_szLocalizationConfig with iHigh
     c. Convert to Unicode, call Ordinal_10004, append to output
   - Else (normal format):
     a. Extract low byte and scale: iCounter = (dwValue & 0xff) * 10 >> 8
     b. Calculate iHigh = dwValue >> 8
     c. If iCounter == 0: format with just iHigh parameter
     d. Else: format with both iHigh and iCounter parameters
     e. Convert result to Unicode, call Ordinal_10004, append to output
6. Call strcat_exref function pointer (stored in EBX/pfnStrcat)
7. Call Ordinal_10004 again
8. Call strcat_exref one final time
9. Return 1 (success)

Parameters:
- nIndex (dword): Resource or string index/selector passed in ECX
- nParam2 (int): Mode selector (0x6 = special handling, 0xdd = alternate path)
- nParam3 (int): Pointer to configuration structure with offsets:
                 +0xdc: shift amount (usually 8)
                 +0xe0: base height/scale value
                 +0xe4: multiplier or divisor
- nParam4 (int): Height or scaling factor (typically decremented for calculation)
- nParam5 (int): Alternate format parameter when non-zero (bitmask or index)

Returns:
- 0 if parameters invalid (both config values at 0xe0/0xe4 are zero)
- 1 if formatting and concatenation successful

Special Cases:
- Magic value 0x100: minimum threshold for small formats
- Magic value 0xc00: threshold triggering large format path
- Ordinal_10004: Called multiple times, likely for string pool/reference management
- Ordinal_578: Unknown ordinal, called with format string for alternate format
- strcat_exref: Function pointer stored in global (likely Unicode::strcat)
- unaff_ESI, unaff_EDI: Unaffected registers containing source/destination strings

Magic Numbers:
- 0x20 (32 decimal): Size of initialization loops for Unicode buffers
- 0xdc: Stack frame size
- 0xe0, 0xe4: Offsets into parameter structure
- 0xc: Return stack cleanup (5 parameters * 2 + 1)
- 0x100: Minimum threshold (256 decimal)
- 0xc00: Large format threshold (3072 decimal)
- 0x6: Special mode indicator
- 0xdd: Alternate format mode indicator
- 0x109f, 0x5511, 0x5300-0x5305: Resource/string pool identifiers

functions.name: CalcImageCoordinates
functions.signature: int CalcImageCoordinates(int * pImageData, int nValue, int * pOutX, int * pOutY, int * pOutMode)
functions.comment:
Calculate image coordinates with zoom and modifier effects.

Note: Function uses 4 stack-allocated temporaries optimized away (uVar3, uVar4, iVar1, iVar2 reused across statements).

Algorithm:
1. Get base delta value via Ordinal_11045 (D2Common.GetUnitStat)
2. Check image mode flag at offset 0x50 (value 0x05 for scaled mode)
3. If scaled mode:
   - Set output mode to 2
   - Get multiplier via Ordinal_11046 (D2Common.GetUnitStat)
   - Multiply by param_2-1, add offset at 0x56
   - Fetch base X/Y at offsets 0x51, 0x52, add delta
   - Left shift by scale factor at 0x4a (masked to 0x1f bits)
   - Multiply by multiplier, right shift by 8 (divide by 256)
4. If standard mode:
   - Fetch base X/Y, add delta
   - Right shift by (8 - scale factor), masked to 0x1f bits
5. Check image type at offset 0x00 (0x14, 0x31, 0x35)
   - If special types, set output X to 1
6. Query game state via FUN_6fb62880 (get world/game context)
   - If state flag at offset +4 == 1:
     - Get skill effect 0x47 via Ordinal_10487 (D2Common.IsSkillActive)
     - If enabled and pImageData null or byte at 0x35 == 0x01:
       - Get party modifier via Ordinal_10949 (query), Ordinal_10968 (apply), Ordinal_10996 (percentage)
       - Apply percentage increase (modifier * result / 100)
     - Repeat for effect 0x48 with offset 0x35 == 0x02

Parameters:
- pImageData: Image/entity structure pointer (nullable for party effects)
- nValue: Dimension/scale parameter (usually width/height)
- pOutX: Output X coordinate (modified by zoom/modifiers)
- pOutY: Output Y coordinate (modified by zoom/modifiers)
- pOutMode: Output mode indicator (2 for scaled, 1 for special types, other for standard)

Returns:
- Last percentage modifier applied, or undefined on standard path

Special Cases:
- NULL pImageData bypasses entity checks (applies global party modifiers)
- Scale factor (offset 0x4a) masked to 5 bits (0-31 valid values)
- Magic values 0x14, 0x31, 0x35 identify special unit types (monst/merc/summon)
- Two skill effects applied in sequence (0x47, 0x48) with conditional party modifiers
- 0x51eb851f constant used for fixed-point division (magic multiplier)

functions.name: GetItemInventorySize
functions.signature: void GetItemInventorySize(int * pWidth, int * pHeight, uint * pFlags, int nBaseWidth, int nBaseHeight, int nSkillId, int nItemParam7, int nItemParam8)
functions.comment:
Calculate item inventory grid dimensions based on item properties, base size, and special modifiers.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input: If nSkillId is 0, log error
2. Get item stat record from game state
3. Determine base dimensions:
   - If nItemParam7 non-zero: fetch from item-specific stat record
   - If nItemParam8 non-zero: get property-based dimensions
   - Otherwise: use default dimensions (0x15, 0x16) with adjustments
4. Apply minimum constraints: width >= 1, height >= 2
5. Add base width and height offsets (0x19, 0x12, 0x11)
6. Calculate width total: add display offset height calculation
7. Check for special effects (0xfe overlay) and add if present
8. If item has properties: add dimensional modifiers for stat 0 and stat 2 (percentage-based)
9. Get bonus property (0x6f) and add to height
10. Check special state flags and set pFlags appropriately
11. Apply final formulas: scale by base dimensions with +100 offset, add bonuses

Parameters:
pWidth - output pointer for final grid width (cells)
pHeight - output pointer for final grid height (cells)
pFlags - output pointer for overlay flags (1=Unique, 3=Unique+Quest)
nBaseWidth - base width offset (usually 0)
nBaseHeight - base height offset (usually 0)
nSkillId - skill ID for lookup (0 triggers error)
nItemParam7 - item parameter 7 (non-zero uses property lookup)
nItemParam8 - item parameter 8 (non-zero uses default dimensions)

Returns:
(void) - outputs via pointer parameters

Special Cases:
- If nSkillId=0: logs error and returns default dimensions
- Ordinal_10966 = D2Common.GetCursorInfo - get cursor object reference
- Ordinal_10807 = D2Common.GetStatValue - property stat 0 (physical damage)
- Ordinal_10808 = D2Common.GetStatValue - property stat 2 (elemental damage)
- Ordinal_10258 = D2Common.GetItemDataRecord - fetch item skill lookup
- Ordinal_10600 = D2Common.ValidateStat - verify item stat exists
- Ordinal_10023 = Storm.Assert - assertion failure handler
- Ordinal_10025 = Storm.Assert - assertion failure handler
- Ordinal_10520 = D2Common.GetItemProperty - fetch bonus property
- Ordinal_10466 = D2Common.GetInventoryImage - get tile overlay spec
- Ordinal_10481 = D2Common.GetAnimationData - fetch animation info
- Ordinal_10996 = D2Common.CalculateDisplayDimension - calculate rendering bounds
- Ordinal_10545 = D2Common.IsItemUnique - check item quality
- Ordinal_10568 = D2Common.GetItemHeight - property height accessor
- Ordinal_10569 = D2Common.GetItemWidth - property width accessor
- Ordinal_10538 = D2Common.IsQuestItem - check quest property
- Ordinal_10968 = D2Common.ApplyOverlay - apply display effect
- Ordinal_10519 = D2Common.GetGameConstant - get constant values (0x11, 0x12, 0x15, 0x16, 0x17, 0x18, 0x19)
- Ordinal_10949 = D2Common.GetCurrentColor - get effect color
- Ordinal_10291 = D2Common.GetItemCategory - determine item type
- Ordinal_11023 = D2Common.CalculateBufferSize - calculate dimensional requirements

functions.name: CalculateAdjustedDimensions
functions.signature: void CalculateAdjustedDimensions(int * pWidth, int * pHeight, uint * pDimensionType, int nParam4, uint * pLookupTable)
functions.comment:
Calculate adjusted width and height dimensions for a game unit based on damage/resistance adjustments.

Algorithm:
1. Get current game state handle via FUN_6fb62880()
2. Loop through damage adjustment table (g_adDamageAdjustment):
   - Fetch adjustment values at current and previous indices via Ordinal_10519
   - Take minimum of both values
   - Accumulate to pWidth and pHeight
   - Update pDimensionType if non-zero adjustment found
3. Apply additional adjustments from properties 0x39, 0x3a, 0x3b:
   - Get property 0x3a (multiplier present flag)
   - If set, fetch properties 0x39 (multiplicand) and 0x3b (multiplier)
   - Calculate scaled adjustment: (multiplier * property) >> 8
   - Accumulate to dimensions and set pDimensionType = 2
4. Clamp pWidth minimum to 1
5. Ensure pHeight > pWidth (increment if needed)
6. If pLookupTable provided, apply special resistance table adjustments:
   - Check game state for valid unit via Ordinal_10966()
   - Verify unit has resistance flag (byte at +0xEB != 0)
   - Loop through resistance adjustment table (g_adResistanceAdjustment):
     - Check if property exists via Ordinal_10466
     - If exists, calculate bonus via Ordinal_11004/11005
     - Accumulate bonuses and set pDimensionType = 3
7. Check for missile properties (Ordinal_10487):
   - If param4 = 0, call Ordinal_10258 with missile data
   - Apply missile adjustment via Ordinal_11038
8. Check for aura presence via Ordinal_10538, set pDimensionType = 3 if found
9. Check for curse via Ordinal_10545, set pDimensionType = 1 if found

Parameters:
- pWidth (ECX): Pointer to width value, accumulated with adjustments
- pHeight (EDX): Pointer to height value, accumulated with adjustments
- pDimensionType (Stack[0x4]): Output dimension type flag (1=curse, 2=property-scaled, 3=aura/resistance)
- nParam4 (Stack[0x8]): Missile parameter flag (0=skip missile prep, !0=process missile)
- pLookupTable (Stack[0xC]): Optional lookup table pointer for special adjustments (may be NULL)

Returns: void (modifies pWidth, pHeight, pDimensionType via pointers)

Special Cases:
- If pWidth < 1, forced to 1 (minimum dimension)
- If pHeight <= pWidth, forced to pWidth + 1
- Resistance table only processed if pLookupTable != NULL
- Magic constants: 0x39, 0x3a, 0x3b are unit property IDs for scaling calculations
- Adjustment tables are fixed global arrays; may represent base stat modifications

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
-------|------|------------|------|-------------
0x0    | 4    | (parameter) | int* | Pointer to width accumulator
0x4    | 4    | (parameter) | int* | Pointer to height accumulator
0x8    | 4    | (parameter) | uint*| Pointer to dimension type flag
0xC    | 4    | (parameter) | int  | Missile parameter flag
0x10   | 4    | (parameter) | uint*| Optional lookup table pointer

functions.name: DrawRangeText
functions.signature: void DrawRangeText(int nMinRange, int nMaxRange, dword dwColorCode, int nXOffset, int nYOffset, int nWidth)
functions.comment:
Draws a formatted range text display at specified screen coordinates.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize Unicode string buffer (64 wide chars) with default constructors
2. Build range text: if min == max use single value format, else use "min-max" format
3. Convert formatted ANSI text to Unicode representation
4. Call Ordinal_10131 with paint data structure pointer
5. Calculate text centering: align within available width
6. Determine vertical position offset based on range bounds
7. Call Ordinal_10127 to prepare rendering context
8. Call DrawCenteredText with calculated coordinates and formatted Unicode text

Parameters:
nMinRange (int ECX) - Minimum value of range display
nMaxRange (int EDX) - Maximum value of range display
dwColorCode (dword Stack[0x4]) - UI color/style code for text rendering
nXOffset (int Stack[0x8]) - Horizontal offset from base screen position
nYOffset (int Stack[0xc]) - Vertical offset from base screen position
nWidth (int Stack[0x10]) - Available width in pixels for centering calculation

Returns:
void - No return value, modifies UI rendering state

Special Cases:
- Single value display (min == max): Uses single-value format string
- Range display (min != max): Uses format string with both values
- Centering calculation uses complex fixed-point math (0x92492493 magic constant)
- Text height adjusted based on range extent difference

Magic Numbers:
0x92492493 - Fixed-point multiplier for text width calculation (dividing by 13)
0x1e0 (480) - Offset for UI Y-coordinate base
0x20 (32) - Unicode buffer element count for loop iteration
0x2 - Unicode character stride (2 bytes per wide char)

functions.name: InitializeSlotResource
functions.signature: void InitializeSlotResource(void * this, int nSlotId, uint * pOutValue1, uint * pOutValue2)
functions.comment:
Initializes slot resource by retrieving stat value and setting output parameters.

1. Get current game state object via FUN_6fb62880
2. Dereference offset 0x84 within state object 
3. Call Ordinal_10258 (D2Common.GetUnitStat) with dereferenced value to obtain stat
4. Initialize first output parameter to zero
5. Initialize second output parameter to zero
6. Call FUN_6fb39c10 with output parameters, stat value, implicit this pointer, and slot ID

nSlotId: Slot or resource identifier
pOutValue1: Pointer to first output value (initialized to 0)
pOutValue2: Pointer to second output value (initialized to 0)

Returns:
void - Sets output parameters via pointers

Special Cases:

- Both output parameters unconditionally initialized to zero before processing

functions.name: CalculateSkillResourceValue
functions.signature: void CalculateSkillResourceValue(int * pOutValue, uint * pOutModifier, uint dwSkillId, uint dwAnotherParam, int nParam5, int nParam6, int nParam7)
functions.comment:
Calculates modified resource cost for skill execution based on unit stats and configurations.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve current unit context and base resource cost
2. Validate param_6 is non-zero (error if zero, logs to g_szSkillHandleError)
3. Determine skill resource type: if nSkillId is zero, fetch from unit offset 0x84
4. Check if skill type equals 0x26 (resource type marker); if match, zero both outputs and jump to LAB_6fb39c80
5. Calculate base modifier: Ordinal_11023(unit, 0, skillId, 0, param_6, 1) returns base
6. Add stat value: Ordinal_10520(unit, 0x77) retrieves additional stat modifier
7. Fetch config data: Ordinal_10966() retrieves global config structure
8. Add scaling from config: multiply (nParam5 - 1) by config[0x124], add config[0x120]
9. Check config validity and byte at offset 0xeb; if set, add Ordinal_10519(unit, 0x145) bonus
10. Percentage calculation: (*pOutValue * total_modifier) / 100 + *pOutValue
11. Reset pOutModifier to 0x00
12. Check Ordinal_10537(unit) - if non-zero, set pOutModifier = 0x03
13. Check Ordinal_10544(unit) - if non-zero, set pOutModifier = 0x01

Parameters:
- pOutValue (int *, ECX): Pointer to output value; initialized with base resource cost from Ordinal_10432
- pOutModifier (uint *, EDX): Pointer to output modifier flags (0x00=normal, 0x01=special, 0x03=bonus)
- nSkillId (uint, [ESP+0x4]): Skill identifier to calculate for
- nAnotherParam (uint, [ESP+0x8]): Additional configuration parameter
- nParam5 (int, [ESP+0xc]): Scaling factor for stat multiplier
- nParam6 (int, [ESP+0x10]): Validation flag (must be non-zero)
- nParam7 (int, [ESP+0x14]): Optional resource type override

Returns:
- void (no return value, modifications made through pointers)
- Side effect: pOutValue contains final calculated cost, pOutModifier contains status flag

Special Cases:
- If nSkillId == 0x26: both outputs zeroed, function returns early
- If nParam6 == 0: logs error via Ordinal_10025 but continues execution
- If nParam7 == 0: attempts to fetch skill type from unit[0x84]
- Config byte at offset 0xeb acts as enable flag for bonus calculation

Magic Numbers:
- 0x26: Skill resource type marker
- 0x84: Offset in unit structure for default skill resource type
- 0x77: Stat identifier for additional modifier lookup
- 0x124: Offset in config structure for scaling multiplier
- 0x120: Offset in config structure for base scaling value
- 0xeb: Offset in config structure for bonus enable flag
- 0x145: Stat identifier for bonus calculation
- 100: Divisor for percentage-based modification calculation
- 0x01: Modifier flag for special state
- 0x03: Modifier flag for bonus state

functions.name: DrawDamageRangeText
functions.signature: void DrawDamageRangeText(dword dwFlags, int * pCoordinates, int nXOffset, dword * pDamageRange, dword dwMinDamage, dword dwMaxDamage, int nBaseX, int nBaseY, int nMaxWidth, int nScreenRowOffset)
functions.comment:
Renders damage range text with dual-range coordinate transformation and internationalization support.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize all coordinate/range variables to zero
2. If screen row offset provided, calculate image-relative coordinates via CalcImageCoordinates
3. Extract zoom factor from coordinate table[0x129]
4. Validate damage range pointer (fatal error if null)
5. Query damage sprite dimensions and adjust ranges via FUN_6fb3a340
6. Apply zoom transformation if both min/max ranges non-zero: result = (value * zoom + rounding) >> 3 + offset
7. Apply zoom transformation to alternate range similarly
8. Branch based on valid range pairs:
   - Both ranges (0,0): draw alternate coordinates
   - Alternate ranges (0,0): draw primary coordinates
   - Both valid: format text strings and draw both centered
9. Format damage text: if min == max, single value; else min-max range
10. Convert ASCII to Unicode via toUnicode
11. Initialize display offset via Ordinal_10127 (D2Common.InitTimingOffset)
12. If offset not set, query game time via Ordinal_10007 and set offset (-6 if time < 6, -7 if time > 9)
13. Draw primary damage text at calculated Y position
14. Draw alternate damage text with secondary offset

Parameters:
dwFlagsMask (ECX) - Drawing flags for text rendering
pCoordinateTable (EDX) - Ptr to coordinate/zoom table containing array at offset 0x129
nZoom - Additional zoom/scale factor
pDamageRange - Ptr to damage range array [min_width, min_height, max_width, max_height]
dwMinDamage - Minimum damage value (32-bit)
dwMaxDamage - Maximum damage value (32-bit)
nBaseX - Base X screen coordinate
nBaseY - Base Y screen coordinate
nMaxWidth - Maximum text width pixels
nRowOffset - Screen row offset for Y positioning

Returns:
void

Note: Function contains 4 SSA variables optimized away by compiler (pUVar2, iVar3, uVar1, local_80 - Unicode array iteration counters and zoom calculation temporaries).

Ordinal Calls:
- Ordinal_10023 (0x6fb3a033): D2Common.AssertFailure - logs assertion with filename, source module, line number
- Ordinal_10127 (0x6fb3a064): D2Common.InitTimingOffset - initializes display offset timing system
- Ordinal_10007 (0x6fb3a0e6): D2Common.GetGameTick - queries current game clock time (6-9 threshold determines offset)

Magic Numbers:
0x129 - Offset within coordinate table for zoom factor
0x5c4 - Error code (assertion line number)
0x20 - Text width in Unicode characters (32)
0x3 - SAR shift count for divide-by-8 scaling
0x7 - Modulo mask for rounding
0x6, 0x9 - Time thresholds for offset calculation
-0x1e0 - Screen height constant offset (-480)
0x1ff - XOR mask (possibly alpha channel)

functions.name: ValidateAndProcessStateChange
functions.signature: dword ValidateAndProcessStateChange(dword * pdwOutVal1, dword * pdwOutVal2, dword nEventId, dword * pdwOutVal3, dword * pdwOutVal4, dword nParam1, dword nParam2, void * pfnCallback, dword nCallbackArg1, dword nCallbackArg2)
functions.comment:
Validates game object state change and executes callback with result handling.

Algorithm:
1. Get current game object context via FUN_6fb62880
2. Check if object state is valid (Ordinal_10462 - context validation)
3. If valid, retrieve state flags from object+0x84 offset
4. Extract state flag #4 and #5 via Ordinal_10257
5. Validate both flags are accessible via Ordinal_10839
6. Check if flags equal 0x26 (VALID_STATE constant) via Ordinal_10751
7. If both flags valid and not 0x26, call FUN_6fb3a4a0 for processing
8. If processing result valid, invoke callback pfnCallback with processed result
9. Call FUN_6fb3a550 for state finaliation
10. If finalization valid, invoke callback again with finalization result
11. On any validation failure, invoke callback with 0x0 (NULL result)
12. Return 1 on success, 0 on early validation failure

Parameters:
- pdwOutVal1: Output pointer for result value 1 (ECX register)
- pdwOutVal2: Output pointer for result value 2 (EDX register)
- nEventId: Event/operation identifier
- pdwOutVal3: Output pointer for intermediate state
- pdwOutVal4: Output pointer for intermediate state
- nParam1: Processing parameter
- nParam2: Processing parameter
- pfnCallback: Callback function pointer (code *) - receives (nParam, nArg1, nArg2, nParam2, nResult)
- nCallbackArg1: First callback argument (typically callback context)
- nCallbackArg2: Second callback argument (callback auxiliary data)

Returns:
- 1: Processing completed (callback invoked, output values set)
- 0: Validation failed early (callback invoked with NULL, no output)

Ordinals Used:
- Ordinal_10462: Context validation check
- Ordinal_10257: State flag extraction by index
- Ordinal_10839: Flag accessibility/validity check
- Ordinal_10751: Flag value query

Callee Functions:
- FUN_6fb62880: Get current game context
- FUN_6fb3a4a0: Process state change (ActivateSecondaryWeaponSlot)
- FUN_6fb3a550: Finalize state (ProcessPlayerInventoryState)

functions.name: ActivateSecondaryWeaponSlot
functions.comment:
Activate secondary weapon slot by validating and switching equipped items.

Algorithm:
1. Validate unit exists using Ordinal_10462 (GetUnitState)
2. Get unit's secondary item reference from offset +0x84
3. Retrieve secondary item data with Ordinal_10258 (GetItemData)
4. Get item type code using Ordinal_10689 (GetItemType)
5. Check if type is 0x04 (dual-wield): set dwWeaponType=5, else 4
6. Equip item with weapon type using Ordinal_10257 (EquipItem)
7. If equipment fails, log error with Ordinal_10023 and exit via FUN_6fb9a10f
8. Check item flag 0x2D using Ordinal_10731 (CheckItemFlag)
9. Validate primary item exists with Ordinal_10839 (GetItemData)
10. Set primary item owned with Ordinal_10524 (SetItemOwned)
11. Set primary item slot 0 with Ordinal_10523 (SetSlotIndex)
12. Validate secondary item exists with Ordinal_10839 (GetItemData)
13. Set secondary item owned with Ordinal_10524 (SetItemOwned)
14. Set secondary item slot 1 with Ordinal_10523 (SetSlotIndex)
15. Return secondary item ID on success

Parameters:
nUnit (int) - Unit pointer, passed in ECX register (fastcall)

Returns:
Secondary item ID (handle) on successful activation
0 on validation failure or equipment errors
-1 on critical error (exits process)

Special Cases:
Item type 0x04 designates dual-wield weapons (uses weapon type 5)
Item type other than 0x04 uses weapon type 4
Flag 0x2D must be present for valid equipment setup
One stack-allocated temporary optimized away during compilation

Note: Function uses 1 stack-allocated temporary optimized away.

functions.name: ProcessPlayerInventoryState
functions.comment:
Validate and process player inventory item state changes

Algorithm:
1. Ordinal_10462: GetPlayerValid(nPlayer) - Validate player exists, return 0 if invalid
2. Load inventory buffer pointer from player+0x84 into dwItemBuf
3. Ordinal_10258: GetItemFromBuffer(dwItemBuf) - Retrieve item from buffer into nResult
4. If nResult==0, return 0 (no item)
5. Ordinal_10689: GetItemQuality(nResult) - Get quality byte into cQuality
6. Compare cQuality==0x04, set dwItemType=0x05 if true, else 0x04
7. Ordinal_10257: SetItemType(dwItemBuf, dwItemType) - Assign type, store in nItem
8. If nItem==0, log error and abort via Ordinal_10023 + FUN_6fb9a10f(0xFFFFFFFF)
9. Ordinal_10731: HasProperty(nItem, 0x2d) - Check for property flag 0x2d into nHasProperty
10. If nHasProperty!=0, proceed to property application:
11.    Ordinal_10839: ValidateItem(nItem) - Validate secondary item
12.    If validation ok, Ordinal_10524: BeginPropertyApplication(nPlayer, nItem)
13.    Then Ordinal_10523: ApplyProperty(nPlayer, nItem, 0)
14.    Ordinal_10839: ValidateItem(nResult) - Validate primary item from step 3
15.    If primary validation ok, Ordinal_10524: BeginPropertyApplication(nPlayer, nResult)
16.    Then Ordinal_10523: ApplyProperty(nPlayer, nResult, 1)
17. Return nResult (item handle, or 0 if property check failed)

Parameters:
- nPlayer (int, ECX): Player unit handle to validate and process

Returns:
- Item handle (int) if successful validation and processing
- 0 if player invalid, no item, or property check failed
- Terminates via FUN_6fb9a10f(0xFFFFFFFF) on SetItemType failure (never returns)

Special Cases:
- Quality 0x04 triggers type 0x05, other qualities use type 0x04
- Property 0x2d initiates dual-item validation and property application chain
- SetItemType failure is fatal - calls error handler
- Both primary and secondary items must validate if property exists

functions.name: ProcessSkillResourceAllocation
functions.signature: void ProcessSkillResourceAllocation(void * this, SkillAllocator * pThis, int nResourceType, dword * pdwResourceValue, dword * pdwResourceFlags, dword * pdwResourceMask, dword * pdwResultFlags)
functions.comment:
Allocate and validate skill resource values based on resource type and state conditions.

Algorithm:
1. Query current game state handle via FUN_6fb62880()
2. Check if state is initialized using Ordinal_10462 (Storm validation - returns non-zero if ready)
3. If initialized (non-zero):
   a. Call ValidateAndProcessStateChange() with resource parameters and current state handle
   b. Return after state validation completes
4. If not initialized (zero):
   a. Query state handle again via FUN_6fb62880()
   b. Load resource configuration from state offset 0x84 via Ordinal_10258 (Storm config accessor)
   c. Clear resource value and flags pointers to 0x00000000
   d. Calculate skill resource allocation using CalculateSkillResourceValue()
   e. Return with allocated values

Parameters:
- pThis: SkillAllocator instance (implicit ECX in __thiscall)
- nResourceType: Resource type identifier for skill allocation
- pdwResourceValue: Output pointer to allocated resource value
- pdwResourceFlags: Output pointer to resource flags configuration
- pdwResourceMask: Output pointer to resource mask value
- pdwResultFlags: Output pointer to result status flags

Returns:
- void (result passed through pointer parameters)

Special Cases:
- State validation via Ordinal_10462 gates between initialized and uninitialized paths
- Offset 0x84 contains resource configuration structure reference
- Both execution paths converge on CalculateSkillResourceValue() with different initial parameters
- Resource value and flags cleared to zero before calculation in uninitialized path

functions.name: CalculateWeaponDamage
functions.signature: void CalculateWeaponDamage(int * pMinDamage, int * pMaxDamage, dword * pSpecialType, dword dwAura, dword dwEnchantBonus, dword dwMastery, int nWeapon)
functions.comment:
Calculate base and enhanced weapon damage with enchantments, auras, and mastery bonuses.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize output values (*pMinDamage = 0, *pMaxDamage = 0)
2. Retrieve game state (nGameState = FUN_6fb62880)
3. Validate weapon handle: if nWeapon == 0, attempt to get from state 0x84 offset
4. Check weapon is equipped (Ordinal_10759 - GetUnitMode): if not equipped, return early
5. Check weapon type (Ordinal_10731 with 0x26 parameter): if type 0x26 is set, process as special case
6. Standard weapon damage path (if not special):
   a. Get damage modifiers (dwAura & 0xff for aura, dwEnchantBonus & 0xff for bonus)
   b. Retrieve skill mastery bonuses (Ordinal_10519): multiply by modifier percentage, divide by 100
   c. Check augmentation flag (0x4e): if set, apply divine damage (Ordinal_11023)
   d. Get base damage values from weapon (Ordinal_10520: 0x9f for min, 0xa0 for max)
   e. Apply damage bonus: (*pMinDamage * nDamageBonus) / 100 + *pMinDamage
   f. Check enhancement flag (0x10): if set, mark special type = 1
   g. Normalize with Ordinal_11038
7. Special weapon damage path (if 0x26 type is set):
   a. Get weapon subtype (Ordinal_10760)
   b. Retrieve subtype damage table (Ordinal_10589)
   c. Initialize character buffer (512 Unicode chars)
   d. Extract offset values from damage table (+0xb0, +0x98, +0xac, +0x94)
   e. Switch on damage type field (+0xa8): determines special type (1/2/3/4)
   f. For type 5 (special): calculate scaled damage based on +0xc0 field / 0x19 (25)
   g. Compute final min/max: scale by bit shift amount at +0x8c, arithmetic right shift by 8

Parameters:
  pMinDamage (int *) - Output minimum damage value
  pMaxDamage (int *) - Output maximum damage value
  pSpecialType (uint *) - Output special damage type (0=normal, 1/2/3/4=special, set if 0x10 flag present)
  dwAura (uint) - Aura effect flags (bits 0-7 contain percentage modifier)
  dwEnchantBonus (uint) - Enchantment bonus flags (bits 0-7 contain percentage modifier)
  dwMastery (uint) - Mastery skill level/bonus
  nWeapon (int) - Weapon handle/ID

Returns:
  void - Results written to pMinDamage, pMaxDamage, pSpecialType pointers

Special Cases:
  - If nWeapon == 0 at start and state 0x84 is also 0, logs error and returns early
  - If weapon not equipped (Ordinal_10759 returns 0), returns early
  - Special weapon types (0x26 flag set) follow alternative calculation path
  - Type 5 special weapons include divisor check: if divisor < 1, force to 1
  - Damage scaling uses magic constant 0x51eb851f (division optimization constant)
  - Final min/max clamped by comparison: if max < min, use max as both

Magic Numbers:
  0x26 - Special weapon type flag identifier
  0x84 - Offset in game state to default weapon
  0x9f, 0xa0 - Offsets for min/max base damage
  0x4e - Augmentation/divine damage flag
  0x10 - Enhancement flag for special type marking
  0x8c - Bit shift amount offset (for damage scaling)
  0xb0, 0x98, 0xac, 0x94 - Damage table offset values
  0xa8 - Damage type field in weapon subtype
  0xc0 - Scaling divisor offset
  0x19 (25) - Base scale divisor
  0x51eb851f - Magic multiplication constant for division (approximately 1/100)
  0xff - Mask to extract flags byte
  0x1f - Bit mask for shift amount validity
  8 - Right shift for final damage normalization

Related Functions:
  - FUN_6fb62880 - Get game state pointer
  - Ordinal_10759 (D2Common.GetUnitMode) - Check if weapon equipped
  - Ordinal_10731 (D2Common.GetUnitStat) - Query weapon property
  - Ordinal_10807/10808 (D2Common.GetUnitStat) - Get aura/bonus flags
  - Ordinal_10519 (D2Common.GetUnitStat) - Get mastery bonus
  - Ordinal_11023 (D2Common.CalcDamage) - Calculate divine damage
  - Ordinal_10520 (D2Common.GetUnitStat) - Get base damage
  - Ordinal_11038 (D2Common.NormalizeDamage) - Finalize damage values
  - Ordinal_10760 (D2Common.GetUnitProperty) - Get weapon subtype
  - Ordinal_10589 (D2Common.GetDataTable) - Retrieve damage table

functions.name: DisplayUnitDamageRange
functions.signature: void DisplayUnitDamageRange(dword dwUnit, int * pScreenPos, int nX, int nY, int nScreenWidth, int nScreenHeight)
functions.comment:
Display damage range text for a unit's equipped weapon(s)

Algorithm:

2. Check if unit can carry two weapons - abort if not dual-wielding capable
3. Determine weapon class from unit item type

dwUnit - Unit ID whose damage will be displayed
